items.title: Gala «African Royality» pour l’éducation des filles : la Fondation Diaka Camara annoncé les couleurs de la 2ème édition
items.description: La Fondation Diaka Camara prépare la deuxième édition de son gala de levée de fonds « African Royality » prévu ce vendredi 6 novembre à Conakry. À cette occasion, la fondatrice et ses partenaires ont animé une conférence de presse ce jeudi 5 novembre 2026. Une opportunité pour présenter les objectifs de ce Gala. À travers la deuxième édition de son gala de levée de fonds « African Royalty », la Fondation Diaka Camara ambitionne de mobiliser davantage de ressources pour soutenir ses différents programmes. C’est dans cette perspective que cette rencontre a réuni plusieurs partenaires de la fondation, dont l’acteur américain Terrence Howard, venu de Los Angeles pour apporter son soutien à cette initiative. Au cours de cette rencontre, Diaka Camara a rappelé que l’éducation des filles et la lutte contre les violences basées sur le genre restent des défis qui dépassent les frontières guinéennes. Elle a notamment insisté sur l’importance de l’engagement collectif et de la mobilisation autour de ces causes. « Donner de l’argent est la chose la plus facile à faire, mais donner de son temps est la chose la plus difficile », a-t-elle souligné, en remerciant les personnes qui accompagnent les activités de la fondation. Parmi les initiatives présentées figure le programme de bourses scolaires Zénab Soumah, baptisé en mémoire de l’ancienne directrice exécutive de la fondation, décédée d’un cancer à l’âge de 30 ans. Dans son exposé, la fondatrice Diaka Camara a expliqué que le nombre de filles bénéficiaires est passé de 47 à 70. La fondation assure leur accompagnement de la maternelle à l’université, notamment à travers la prise en charge des frais de scolarité, des uniformes, des fournitures et de la cantine. Des cours d’anglais et d’informatique sont également prévus pour renforcer leurs compétences. La construction de bibliothèques scolaires constitue un autre axe majeur de son intervention. Lancé en 2018, le programme « Une école, une bibliothèque » ambitionne de construire 15 bibliothèques dans le Grand Conakry. À ce jour, quatre ont été réalisées ou engagées, selon la fondatrice. Parmi elles figurent celles du lycée 2-Octobre, de Château d’Eau et du 1er-Mars, réalisée avec l’appui de la Fondation Orange. Un autre projet concerne l’école primaire Général Lansana Conté de Dubréka, qui accueille environ 1 600 élèves répartis dans huit bâtiments. Sa rénovation doit être inaugurée après le gala, au mois de novembre. La fondation intervient également dans la lutte contre les violences basées sur le genre à travers sa campagne « Brisons le silence ». Diaka Camara a expliqué que certaines victimes renoncent à porter plainte en raison de leur dépendance financière ou de la précarité de leurs conditions de vie. Pour les accompagner, la structure prend notamment en charge des frais médicaux, des consultations psychologiques et des frais juridiques pour les femmes qui souhaitent engager des poursuites contre leurs agresseurs. Présente à cette conférence, la représentante du ministère des Sports, Marawa Touré, chef de cabinet du département, a justifié le partenariat avec le gala par le rôle éducatif du sport. « Le sport va au-delà des compétitions et de l’exercice physique. C’est aussi une façon de se dépasser, de donner de soi et de s’auto-éduquer », a-t-elle déclaré. De son côté, Malick Kébé directeur du FODAC a insisté sur le lien entre l’éducation, la culture, le sport et la jeunesse. Pour lui, aucun développement durable ne peut se construire sans un investissement dans le capital humain. Il a également rappelé que le sport transmet des valeurs essentielles comme la discipline, le respect et la rigueur. Au-delà de la mobilisation financière, cette deuxième édition d’African Royality entend ainsi fédérer des personnalités du monde culturel, sportif et économique autour d’un objectif commun : améliorer les conditions d’accès à l’éducation et offrir de meilleures perspectives aux jeunes filles. Pour la Fondation Diaka Camara, l’enjeu est de poursuivre les actions engagées et de renforcer leur portée auprès des communautés.

items.title: Video: Surveillance footage shows suspects dumping body of 24-year-old Ghanaian, Joseph Owusu, in New York
items.description: Surveillance footage has emerged showing two unidentified individuals removing the body of 24-year-old Ghanaian Joseph Owusu from the boot of a white saloon car and abandoning it in the Bronx in New York. The footage, sighted on Friday, November 6, 2026, and shared by American broadcaster ABC7, shows the two individuals unloading a large black duffel bag from the vehicle during the night. They are seen dragging the bag onto the pavement before driving away. Further footage from the following day captures another man placing the bag on a metal stretcher and wheeling it away. Owusu’s body was later discovered by a man searching for scrap metal, with his family and Ghanaian officials subsequently identifying him as the deceased. His death has left his family devastated, with his brother, Kojo Yeboah, appealing for justice and answers about the circumstances surrounding the incident. “I need justice for Joseph. I want the truth to come out because my brother didn’t deserve to die the way he did. He’s only 24. He had a lot of living to do,” he said. Yeboah, who was shown the surveillance footage, said he could not identify the individuals captured removing his brother’s body, despite watching the video several times in search of possible clues. “No, I don’t recognise anybody. I wish, but these people are just people I’ve never seen before,” he said. He added that he had shared the footage with his brother’s friends in the hope that someone might recognise the individuals or provide information that could assist the investigation. Describing his brother’s character, Yeboah said Owusu was widely loved and had a deep passion for music and the church. He revealed that the 24-year-old served as an organist at their church in the Bronx and could spend several hours playing the piano to perfect his performance. “He was loved by everyone. He would play the piano for hours and hours and just make sure that he didn’t make a mistake,” he said. According to the family, Owusu worked providing direct support to people with disabilities while pursuing studies in computer science. His brother said the family was struggling to come to terms with his sudden death, particularly the absence of someone who had been an important part of their everyday lives. He said he was also trying to remain strong for their mother, who has been deeply affected by the loss. The family is now appealing for justice as investigations continue into the circumstances surrounding Owusu’s death and the identities of those captured in the surveillance footage. Owusu’s reported death comes barely a few days after 15-year-old Ghanaian Javits Frimpong was also shot dead in Bronx.

items.title: Hawa Koomson warns against shielding Obuasi SHTS headmaster in alleged sexual assault case
items.description: The National Women’s Organiser of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Mavis Hawa Koomson, has cautioned traditional, political and religious leaders against interfering with investigations into alleged sexual assaults involving the Headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School, Abdulai Zakaria. According to her, some individuals are attempting to influence victims and their families to withdraw from the case, warning that such actions could undermine efforts to secure justice for the alleged victims. “Somebody is deliberately shielding him. We have people who are going around pleading with the parents not to allow their children to take the matter up,” she said. Mrs Koomson made the remarks while leading a protest by the NPP Women’s Wing in Obuasi to demand justice for 19 girls allegedly sexually abused by the headmaster. Speaking to JoyNews’ Nana Yaw Gyimah on Friday, November 6, she appealed to parents who had reportedly withdrawn their children from the case to allow them to cooperate with investigators and testify in court. She alleged that some parents had been approached and persuaded not to pursue the matter, raising concerns about possible witness interference. “Why are they shielding Zakaria Abdulai? Is it because he’s an NDC man? Is it because they are giving them 1,000 cedis to keep quiet?” she asked. Mrs Koomson further claimed that two of the alleged victims had gone to the police station with their father to withdraw their statements after discussions involving the father’s family and the headmaster’s lawyer. She expressed concern that the alleged victims could be denied justice if pressure continued to be exerted on their families. The NPP Women’s Organiser also appealed to members of the Hausa community to encourage the affected families to allow the girls to speak out, insisting that sexual harassment was condemned by religious teachings, including the Quran. She maintained that the protest was part of efforts to ensure accountability and justice for the alleged victims, adding that the NPP Women’s Wing would not abandon the campaign. “We’ll still continue with the demonstration. We have a lot of plans on the way until justice is given to the girls,” she said. Mrs Koomson also called on all individuals with information about the alleged incidents to support the process rather than take actions that could compromise the pursuit of justice.

items.title: Bas mono/Aménagement des pistes rurales: Des populations riveraines sensibilisées sur le plan d’action de réinstallation
items.description: Afagnan, 6 nov. (ATOP) – Une équipe du ministère en charge des Pistes rurales a sensibilisé les populations et chefs des services déconcentrés de l’état sur le Plan d’action de réinstallation et de réinsertion (PARR) des personnes lors d’une tournée d’informations, effectuée du 4 au 6 novembre à Afagnan. Cette démarche s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet de réhabilitation et de réaménagement des pistes rurales au Togo. Ledit projet est porté par le gouvernement à travers le ministère en charge des Pistes rurales. Il bénéficie du soutien technique et financier volontaire de la banque allemande de développement (KFW) et de l’Agence français de développement (AFD). L’ambition est de réaménager au moins 1000 km sur toute l’étendue du territoire national. Les assises ont permis d’informer les populations sur les objectifs du projet et son principe, le mode de mise en œuvre du PARR des personnes affectées par le projet. Il s’agit aussi de recueillir les préoccupations, les suggestions, les avis, et les doléances des populations. Les échanges ont porté sur le recensement des biens dans les emprises, la prise en compte des personnes affectées notamment le système de donation volontaire pour les biens mineurs qui seront impactés dans les emprises. Les discussions ont, aussi, axé sur la protection de l’environnement, les risques d’accidents, de violences basées sur le genre, les impacts négatifs, la pollution de l’environnement et les comportements à adopter pendant les travaux. Le chef de l’équipe, Akakpo Kokouda, consultant sur l’aspect social pour la réalisation des travaux, a invité les populations à s’impliquer pleinement pour la réussite du projet. Selon lui, ce projet vise à désenclaver les localités, à faciliter l’écoulement des produits agricoles et à améliorer l’accès des populations aux soins sociaux de base. Il a indiqué que dans les agglomérations, les pistes vont mesurer 8 m et 12 m dans les campagnes. Dans la préfecture de Bas-Mono, cinq pistes sont concernées à savoir, les pistes reliant (Anfoin-Attitogon-Afagnan), (Tokplie-Agomé-Glozou), (Afagnan Gbleta-Kpetsou-Dzrekpo Hagou), (Afagnagan- Logowomé-Masseda) et (klologo-Momé Gbavé-Afagnan). Sur ces axes, il est prévu des travaux d’ouverture, de reprofilage, de chargement systématique de gravier, de construction d’ouvrage de franchissement et d’entretien courant. ATOP/DK/DHK

items.title: CRIEF : Général Mathurin Bangoura et ses co-prévenus attendus le 16 décembre prochain
items.description: Sauf changement de dernière minute, les débats dans le procès opposant le parquet spécial à l’ancien gouverneur de la ville de Conakry, le général Mathurin Bangoura et ses co-prévenus devraient s’ouvrir le mercredi 16 décembre 2026. Cette décision émane de la chambre de jugement de la Cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières (CRIEF), présidée par Alpha Camara. Les prévenus, Mathurin Bangoura, Mori Diané et la Société guinéenne des mines SA, sont poursuivis à la suite d’une plainte de la société Réma Tip Top Guinea SARL. Ils répondent de faits présumés d’escroquerie, d’abus de confiance, de faux et usage de faux en écriture authentique et de commerce, ainsi que d’entrave aux droits d’un actionnaire de participer à une assemblée générale. Lors de l’audience du 4 novembre dernier, les prévenus ont brillé par leur absence. Face à cette situation, la cour a renvoyé l’affaire au 16 décembre prochain pour leur comparution. Il convient de préciser qu’une seconde procédure opposant les deux parties est également pendante devant la même juridiction. Dans ce volet, le général Mathurin Bangoura, Mori Diané et la Société guinéenne des mines SA poursuivent à leur tour la société Réma Tip Top Guinée SA, ainsi qu’Alpha Oumar Bah et Abdoulaye Barry, pour des faits présumés d’escroquerie et de complicité d’escroquerie. Cette seconde affaire a également été renvoyée au 16 décembre prochain pour la comparution des prévenus. items.title: An Absolute Beauty
items.description: Pity the Canadian book reviewer in the autumn of 1980. An American publisher has announced, with some fanfare, a forthcoming title about the national pastime—the Canadian national pastime. Amazons: An Intimate Memoir by the First Woman Ever to Play in the National Hockey League promises to tell the story of Cleo Birdwell’s debut season with the New York Rangers. Of course, as a Canadian in good standing, you know that no woman has ever played in the NHL; there is no Cleo Birdwell. But the people behind the book are committed to the bit. At the Canadian Booksellers Association convention, held that summer in Toronto, a leggy model impersonated Birdwell, signing advance copies in a Rangers jersey. “She’s tough and sexy,” the book’s publisher whispered to a Globe and Mail reporter. Clearly this book demands attention. Perhaps the charade might even provide a welcome distraction after Canada’s rather unmiraculous sixth-place finish at Lake Placid. But what awaits within its pages confounds. The on-ice action is overshadowed by ever more elaborate accounts of Birdwell’s sexual adventures. In the course of one season, she sleeps with the Rangers’ head coach, the Rangers’ general manager, a former Rangers player, and one very jet-lagged tennis star. This is an incomplete list. In the brutal assessment of one critic in Calgary, Amazons is “little more than hardcover softcore porn that will disappoint hockey fans and heavy breathers alike.” But Amazons wasn’t smut, or not exactly. Its author was Don DeLillo. His publisher took pains to guard this secret, but there was no disguising his writing from those who already admired it. Colin McEnroe , reviewing the book for the Hartford Courant , seems to have been the first to identify DeLillo’s authorship in print. “ ‘Amazons’ is not only his book,” he wrote. “It’s his best book.” DeLillo did not share this appraisal. Although the book sold well—better, in fact, than any of his previous novels—he would not allow it to be republished. Even after the breakout success of White Noise in 1985, it never appeared in his official bibliography. Amazons soon faded into obscurity. I first learned of its existence in 2006, when the writer Keith Gessen published an essay in The New York Times Book Review titled “ In Search of the Great American Hockey Novel .” Gessen wrote of his dismay that hockey had not produced a literature as rich as that of boxing or baseball. “Where is the Chekhov of the Chicago Blackhawks?” he asked. “Who is the Stendhal of the stick to the groin?” On the shelf dedicated to immortal hockey books, Gessen placed just two volumes: Ken Dryden’s melancholy 1983 memoir, The Game , about his final season with the dynastic Montreal Canadiens, and DeLillo’s Amazons . Hockey and literature were two pursuits struggling to find an audience; perhaps, Gessen ventured, they could help each other. “What is needed now, for the sake of both hockey and literature, is more hockey literature,” he wrote. “Not just books about hockey, like ‘The Game,’ but also books not about hockey, like ‘Amazons’—which is not about hockey in just the right way.” Gessen may have been only half serious, but two decades after his essay appeared, something like his modest proposal has come to pass. The Intangibles , a new memoir by the New Yorker staff writer Nick Paumgarten, is a worthy successor to The Game , no less so for describing a career played in bruising beer leagues. The success of Heated Rivalry on HBO Max has made Rachel Reid’s queer-romance series, from which it was adapted, into a publishing juggernaut. Hockey erotica, once a fringe category, has become a cottage industry. Following that unlikely turn of events—and a January story in the Times positing DeLillo as the genre’s unlikely inventor—his editor and agent entreated him to allow Amazons back into print. DeLillo acquiesced. After 46 years, Cleo Birdwell is finally making her curtain call. A mazons was not DeLillo’s first foray into the world of sport. That distinction belongs to End Zone , his heady 1972 novel about college football and the madness of mutual assured destruction. Later, in the prologue to Underworld (1997), he turned to baseball, with his panoramic account of Bobby Thomson’s “shot heard ’round the world.” In those pages, too, nuclear war hangs in the air; the White House announced on the same day in 1951 that the Soviet Union had conducted a bomb test. The tone of Amazons is zanier, more absurd, untroubled by nuclear annihilation. If anything hangs in the air, it’s the reek of the hockey bag. Cleo Birdwell is the pride of Badger, Ohio, which she describes as a small, straightforward town where “the school was on School Street, the bank was on Bank Street, the river ran by River Road.” But Cleo is not an ingenue; she’s a hockey player. No amount of towel snapping or jock talk seems capable of making her blush. On the contrary, she’s a wry raconteur of her teammates’ puerile antics. One player, Eric Torkleson, has such an enormous member that it becomes an honorary Ranger, known as Torkle. “A player would say, ‘How’s Torkle doing today?’ Or, ‘Who’s playing Torkle in the movie version?’ Or, ‘Is it true Torkle’s being asked to endorse Jimmy Carter?’ ” The book is as sex-drenched as the Calgary reviewer warned. But sex functions less as titillation and more as the engine of the satire. Its object, mostly, is the American male. Cleo is frank, confident, liberated; her lovers are neurotic and narcissistic. One, the Rangers’ general manager, is unable to perform after Cleo makes an offhanded Watergate joke. How could he, having been reminded of this great blow to the male ego? “We lost our manhood, our sense of pride and honor, our belief in God and Dick Nixon, our deepest dreams, hopes, and ambitions.” (In an earlier scene, the GM has been deflated by intrusive thoughts of Torkle.) Men who aren’t trying to sleep with Cleo are usually trying to persuade her to sell something—the rank commercialization of sport is one of the novel’s many prescient targets. Cleo is asked to hawk a sensual whirlpool bath called the Primal Vortex and a snack food called Amazons, especially formulated for “every age, every size, every make of woman.” She refuses both endorsements. In the middle of the Rangers’ season, Hughes Tool, the conglomerate that owns the team, hires a Saudi national to run it, hoping to push through a business deal with “men in the Gulf.” DeLillo seems to have anticipated our age of sportswashing, too. To be clear, Amazons is not a lost masterpiece. Some scenes drag, like runaway SNL sketches. The dialogue, although generally hilarious, can take on a rim-shot quality, as if DeLillo were doing Dangerfield. A sportswriter confesses to Cleo that his ex-wife is now a lesbian. “Who is she a lesbian with?” she asks. “Paine, Webber, Jackson and Curtis. She’s a financial analyst.” Robert Gottlieb, DeLillo’s editor at the time, turned down Amazons . You wonder how the man who convinced Joseph Heller that Catch‑22 sounded funnier than Catch‑18 might have sharpened this manuscript. [ From the May 1973 issue: “The Bucky Wunderlick Story,” by Don DeLillo ] As for the hockey quotient, some fans may wish that DeLillo had set more of the novel between the boards. But Amazons is like Dickie Dunn’s newspaper accounts of the Charlestown Chiefs in Slap Shot : It captures the spirit of the thing. The locker-room banter, at once clever and cretinous; the relentless travel to frozen, past-their-prime cities; the vicious play of the Philadelphia Flyers and the bloodlust of their fans (“screaming made-up and never-before-heard obscenities, as though they were overwhelmed by a massive thyroid deficiency”); the otherworldly allure of a sport conducted, improbably, on a sheet of ice. “In a way it is the most romantic game,” the Rangers’ head coach, Jean-Paul Larousse, says. “There is a lightness, a speed without effort. It is the skates.” It was lightness and speed that drew Nick Paumgarten to hockey. On land, he was ungainly: “You run like a goof,” his brother once told him. “But on the ice the hobbles fell away. With skates on my feet, I could glide, swerve, cut, and feel for a few seconds at least that I’d broken the code, whatever it was.” Paumgarten grew up playing hockey in New York City. His junior career petered out in prep school, but for much of his adult life, he’s competed in Manhattan’s beer leagues. He’s played on ragtag teams with only-in–New York linemates: creative types, a master crane rigger, a guy who used to be Woody Allen’s super. Some are ringers fresh out of college; others are graybeards holding on for one more season of glory. Not that there is much glory to be had when the puck drops at 11:30 p.m. on the far west side. “We did it for no one but ourselves, and really it was more like we were doing it to ourselves,” he writes in The Intangibles . “It was more destructive than constructive: murderous to our daylight ambitions and obligations, hard on the joints, and maybe equally hard on our families and friends.” So why do it? For fellowship, for laughs, for escape, for the spirit of the thing. To find what hockey players call the absolute beauties, like-minded men who play the right way: “with a commitment not just to proper comportment and teamwork but also to sticking around for postgame beers and high- and low-minded banter. A sense of humor, a sense of absurdity.” The Intangibles, the team that gives the memoir its name, plays the right way. It has some elite skaters but also plenty of grinders, the guys you can count on to show up, hustle, and, if necessary, intimidate the opposition, like the maniacal Flyers of old. The license to exact a measure of retribution for a cheap shot or a high stick, for running up the score or running your mouth—this, too, is part of hockey’s ethos, and its appeal to men arriving at the rink from jobs, white collar or blue, that may offer fewer opportunities to administer just deserts. Paumgarten himself is not above such belligerent displays. “On the ice,” he writes, “in this realm circumscribed by boards and Plexiglas and patrolled by men in stripes, an artificial universe where you dart around in a suit of armor, with wings on your feet and levers in your hands, it is a privilege and a joy to shove and slash and tell people to fuck off, to be a jerk to strangers, without it being in any way an actionable affront.” Someone tell Keith Gessen: We have found the Stendhal of the stick to the groin. Though I suspect he already knows this. One of the Intangibles is a writer, referred to only as Keith, who often composes arch postgame emails, recording for posterity the team’s triumphs and follies. I’m pretty sure I recognize the voice. This article appears in the December 2026 print edition with the headline “An Absolute Beauty.”

items.title: ‘My biggest fear is the loss of lives’: NPA Chief warns against fuel siphoning
items.description: The Chief Executive of the National Petroleum Authority (NPA), Godwin Kudzo Tameklo, has delivered a heartfelt appeal to Ghanaians to protect their lives by staying away from overturned fuel tankers, warning that the temptation to collect petroleum products from accident scenes could lead to irreversible tragedy. Speaking at the 2026 NPA Consumer Week celebration in Kasoa on Thursday, November 5, Mr Tameklo cautioned against the dangerous practice of gathering at accident scenes to siphon fuel. “My biggest fear is the loss of lives,” he said, explaining that property could be recovered while the loss of a human life was irreversible. His warning echoes the NPA’s established “Stay Back, Stay Safe” campaign, which discourages fuel siphoning and dangerous gatherings at tanker accident scenes. The Authority’s published safety guidance also cautions people against approaching such scenes to take photographs or videos, advising the public to leave the response to trained professionals, including the Ghana National Fire Service and the Police. Mr Tameklo urged residents to allow the appropriate authorities to handle tanker emergencies and warned against encouraging others to collect fuel.

items.title: Cashew crisis: Usibras imports Ivorian kernels to save Ghanaian jobs
items.description: In a dramatic shift highlighting systemic pressures on domestic agro-processors, leading Ghanaian cashew processor Usibras has turned to importing semi-processed cashew kernels from neighboring Côte d’Ivoire to keep its factory operational. The decision comes after soaring domestic farm-gate prices and aggressive foreign buying rendered local raw cashew nut procurement highly uncompetitive. To sustain factory activity, Usibras has resorted to importing borma kernels cashew nuts that have been shelled and dried but retain their inner skin for final peeling, processing, and packaging in Ghana. The emergency supply chain pivot underscores a severe operational mismatch between processing infrastructure and raw material availability. During the last harvest season, Usibras managed to purchase only 6,500 tonnes of raw cashew nuts (RCN). This procurement volume represents a mere 19 per cent of the company’s installed processing capacity of 35,000 tonnes per annum. Operating at less than one-fifth of its potential has placed immense financial strain on the facility, threatening the viability of one of West Africa’s largest cashew processing investments. Unregulated Raw Exports Create Uneven Playing Field Usibras leadership points to significant regulatory gaps as the primary catalyst for the crisis. Under current trade regulations, raw cashew nuts can be exported from Ghana virtually unrestricted, with traders paying only a nominal levy of GH¢92 per tonne to the Tree Crops Development Authority (TCDA). This regulatory structure permits foreign buying agents to purchase raw nuts directly from farming communities at aggressive prices. Because foreign buyers export raw materials without value addition, they avoid local operational overheads, power tariffs, and labor costs allowing them to outbid domestic processors who bear the heavy capital expenditure of local manufacturing. “We want to buy from Ghanaian farmers and process their cashew here in Ghana. But we cannot compete when raw nuts leave the country almost tax-free. Without policies that support local processing, jobs and rural incomes will continue to suffer,” Job Cuts and Threat of Total Market Exit in 2027 The economic ramifications of the procurement shortfall have had a direct impact on local employment. Faced with severe underutilization of its processing capacity, Usibras was forced to reduce its workforce by 50 per cent, from 700 to 350 employees. Company management has warned that further job cuts may become inevitable if conditions in the domestic raw cashew market do not improve. The potential absence of Usibras from Ghana’s domestic raw cashew nut market in 2027 could result in an estimated US$17 million in lost direct purchasing expenditure. This represents money that would otherwise be injected into cashew-growing communities through purchases from Ghanaian farmers. Beyond the immediate loss of income for farmers, the withdrawal of such a significant buyer would have wider economic consequences for rural communities. Local traders, transport operators, service providers and other businesses that depend on the cashew value chain would also experience reduced economic activity. Usibras has emphasized that its position should not be interpreted as a withdrawal of support for Ghanaian farmers. Rather, it reflects prevailing market conditions and regulatory imbalances that have made the domestic procurement of raw cashew nuts economically unsustainable for local processors. Crucially, company officials have indicated that Usibras could withdraw entirely from Ghana’s raw cashew nut market during the 2027 season if farm-gate prices remain above levels that allow for economically viable domestic processing. Without urgent government intervention to address the regulatory and market imbalances between domestic processors and raw cashew exporters, Ghana risks losing more than industrial jobs and local value addition. The country also stands to forfeit millions of dollars in direct investment in farming communities, further weakening rural livelihoods and the broader economic benefits generated by the cashew industry. Urgent Policy Interventions Demanded to Protect Value Addition A prolonged exit by major industrial buyers like Usibras poses severe long-term risks to Ghana’s agricultural sector. While foreign traders offer short-term price spikes, local processors provide guaranteed, year-round off-take agreements and industrial jobs essential for rural economic stability. Industry stakeholders are urging government authorities to introduce targeted protective measures. Proposed interventions include implementing differential export duties on raw nuts, establishing local processing quotas, and offering utility subsidies to level the playing field against foreign raw nut exporters. Without decisive policy action, Ghana risks transforming from a prospective regional processing hub into a mere exporter of low-value raw agricultural commodities. Established in Brazil in 1979, Usibras expanded into Africa in 2008 before setting up its Ghana operations. The company began constructing ones biggest factory in West Africa its cashew processing factory at Prampram in 2013, with an investment of more than 15 million dollars. The facility commenced operations in November 2014 to process cashew nuts into finished products for local and international markets.

items.title: Fonds Mohammed VI pour l’investissement : 7,2 MMDH pour soutenir l’économie productive
items.description: Le Fonds Mohammed VI pour l’investissement (FM6I) a mobilisé 7,2 milliards de dirhams (MMDH) de fonds propres à fin 2025 et accompagné 52 entreprises, selon son premier rapport d’impact. Avec un objectif de 120 MMDH d’investissements sur cinq ans, l’institution entend renforcer le financement des entreprises et des projets stratégiques. Un enjeu demeure toutefois : mieux répartir les investissements entre les régions, alors que l’axe Casablanca-Rabat concentre encore près de 58,5 % des flux recensés. Le FM6I entend jouer un rôle accru dans le financement de l’économie nationale et la mobilisation des capitaux privés. À fin 2025, l’institution avait mobilisé 7,2 MMDH de fonds propres dans le cadre de ses interventions destinées à soutenir l’investissement productif, les entreprises et les projets stratégiques. Ces résultats figurent dans son premier rapport d’impact au titre de l’année 2025. Le document fait état de 52 entreprises financées et d’un périmètre d’intervention couvrant dix des douze régions du Royaume. Les projets soutenus ont également contribué à accompagner plus de 15.000 emplois. Créé avec un capital initial de 15 MMDH, le Fonds s’est fixé pour ambition de mobiliser 120 milliards de dirhams d’investissements au cours des cinq prochaines années. Une ambition qui repose notamment sur sa capacité à attirer des investisseurs nationaux et internationaux, en complément de ses propres ressources. Un effet de levier sur les capitaux privés Le modèle d’intervention du Fonds repose sur trois mécanismes : l’investissement direct, la participation indirecte à travers des fonds spécialisés et les instruments de financement par dette subordonnée. Ces dispositifs permettent de diriger les ressources vers plusieurs secteurs considérés comme prioritaires, notamment l’industrie, les infrastructures, l’agriculture, le tourisme, les petites et moyennes entreprises ainsi que l’innovation. L’un des principaux enseignements du rapport concerne l’effet de levier généré par ces interventions. Chaque dirham investi dans le cadre des opérations en fonds propres privés a permis de mobiliser 4,3 dirhams supplémentaires auprès d’autres investisseurs. Pour les financements accordés à travers les instruments de dette subordonnée, ce rapport atteint 5,4 dirhams mobilisés pour chaque dirham engagé par le Fonds. Dans le détail, les fonds d’investissement soutenus ont atteint une taille cible globale de 18,7 MMDH . Sur ce montant, 14,4 milliards ont été mobilisés auprès d’investisseurs nationaux et internationaux, tandis que la contribution du Fonds s’est élevée à 4,4 MMDH. Les investissements effectivement orientés vers les entreprises ont atteint 3,9 milliards de dirhams, au bénéfice de 27 sociétés. Au total, 50 investisseurs nationaux et étrangers ont participé à ces opérations. Ils regroupent notamment des caisses de retraite, des banques, des compagnies d’assurance, de grands groupes, des institutions de financement du développement et des fonds souverains. Les investisseurs marocains représentent 64 % de cette base, contre 36 % pour les investisseurs étrangers. Le recours à la dette subordonnée constitue un autre levier de financement, particulièrement pour les entreprises qui ont besoin de ressources complémentaires aux crédits bancaires classiques. Le Fonds a engagé 1,2 MMDH à travers cet instrument, contribuant à attirer 2,6 MMDH de fonds propres supplémentaires et à soutenir un portefeuille de projets représentant un investissement global prévisionnel de 6,6 MMDH. Cette formule a permis l’approbation du financement de 85 projets. Elle a contribué au soutien de 7.120 emplois, avec 4.130 postes supplémentaires attendus. Elle vise notamment à faciliter les projets d’extension, le renouvellement des équipements et le renforcement des capacités productives des PME, grâce à des conditions de financement adaptées à leurs besoins. L’énergie et les infrastructures parmi les investissements stratégiques Le rapport met également en avant l’intervention du Fonds dans des infrastructures considérées comme stratégiques pour l’économie nationale, notamment dans le secteur énergétique. L’une des opérations citées concerne la centrale électrique de Tahaddart, dont le Fonds a acquis une participation globale de 52 %, à la suite du rachat de parts détenues par Siemens et Endesa, respectivement à hauteur de 20 % et 32 %. D’une capacité de production de 400 mégawatts, cette centrale contribue à couvrir des besoins électriques équivalant à la consommation d’environ 600.000 foyers. Son taux de disponibilité atteint 99,8 %, selon les données du rapport. Cette opération s’inscrit dans une logique de renforcement de la sécurité énergétique et de consolidation des infrastructures électriques du Royaume. Le document revient également sur le partenariat stratégique conclu en mai 2025 entre le FM6I, TAQA Morocco et Nareva, en coordination avec le gouvernement et l’Office national de l’électricité et de l’eau potable. Ce partenariat prévoit la mobilisation d’environ 130 milliards de dirhams d’investissements à l’horizon 2030. Les projets envisagés portent sur le développement de nouvelles capacités de production électrique à partir du gaz naturel et des énergies renouvelables, le renforcement du réseau de transport d’électricité ainsi que la réalisation d’infrastructures de dessalement et de transfert d’eau. Les objectifs mentionnés comprennent notamment des capacités de dessalement de 900 millions de mètres cubes et de transfert de 800 millions de mètres cubes d’eau. Ces investissements doivent contribuer à répondre à la progression des besoins énergétiques et hydriques du pays, dans un contexte marqué par les contraintes liées au stress hydrique. L’emploi et l’équilibre territorial en ligne de mire L’impact des interventions du Fonds se mesure également à travers leur contribution à l’emploi. Plus de 15.000 postes ont été soutenus dans le cadre des projets accompagnés, avec une répartition entre les différents mécanismes de financement. Les investissements dans les actifs privés représentent environ la moitié des emplois concernés, tandis que les instruments de dette subordonnée en comptabilisent près de 36 %. Le rapport replace ces résultats dans un contexte de fortes tensions sur le marché du travail. Il rappelle que le taux de chômage au Maroc a atteint 13 % en 2025, avec un niveau de 37,2 % chez les jeunes, tandis que le taux d’activité s’est établi à 43,5 %. Des indicateurs qui soulignent l’importance de soutenir les activités productives et les projets susceptibles de générer des emplois durables. La dimension territoriale constitue toutefois l’un des principaux défis identifiés dans le document. Si les interventions du Fonds couvrent désormais dix régions sur douze, la répartition des investissements demeure marquée par une forte concentration géographique. L’axe Casablanca-Rabat absorbe ainsi près de 58,5 % des investissements recensés. Cette situation pose la question de la capacité des mécanismes de financement à irriguer davantage les régions qui attirent moins spontanément les capitaux privés. Pour le Fonds, la réduction des disparités territoriales passe par le développement de projets capables de valoriser les ressources locales, de structurer les chaînes de production et de renforcer l’attractivité économique des territoires, notamment dans l’industrie, l’agriculture et le tourisme. L’enjeu ne consiste donc pas uniquement à augmenter les montants mobilisés, mais aussi à améliorer leur répartition et leur contribution au développement régional. Des critères de durabilité dans les investissements Le rapport aborde enfin les aspects liés à la gouvernance et à la durabilité. Selon le document, l’ensemble des investissements a fait l’objet d’une évaluation au regard des critères environnementaux, sociaux et de gouvernance (ESG). Les sociétés de gestion concernées sont également engagées dans des programmes visant à améliorer leurs pratiques dans ces domaines. Le Fonds fait par ailleurs état de partenariats avec des institutions internationales, dont la Banque européenne d’investissement et l’Union européenne, afin de soutenir l’investissement durable et d’accompagner les entreprises marocaines dans l’amélioration de leurs performances. The post Fonds Mohammed VI pour l’investissement : 7,2 MMDH pour soutenir l’économie productive appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Gender Minister pushes for greater economic opportunities for women at 2026 Commonwealth Women’s Forum
items.description: The Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, has called for practical interventions to help women expand their businesses, access finance and take greater control of their economic future. She made the call at the 2026 Commonwealth Women’s Forum in St John’s, Antigua and Barbuda, where she outlined Ghana’s policy measures and experiences in promoting women’s economic empowerment. Speaking during a session on women’s economic empowerment, which brought together government representatives, private sector players and development partners, Dr Lartey stressed that empowering women economically was essential not only for social development but also for national growth. “Women do not only take part in institutions, but we also lead,” she said, highlighting the growing role of women in leadership and the need to create more opportunities for their participation in economic activities. The Minister outlined several policy initiatives Ghana is implementing to strengthen women’s economic participation. These include the National Gender Policy 2025–2034, the National Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Policy, the National Financial Inclusion and Development Strategy, the National E-Commerce Strategy 2025–2029 and the 24-Hour Economy Policy. She said these initiatives were supported by the Affirmative Action (Gender Equity) Act, 2024, which provides a legal framework for advancing gender equality. However, Dr Lartey cautioned that policy commitments must translate into tangible improvements in women’s lives, noting that many Ghanaian women entrepreneurs continue to face challenges despite their significant contribution to the economy. She identified limited access to finance, the concentration of women-owned businesses in the informal sector and inadequate connections to markets, buyers and investors as some of the barriers restricting business growth. “Women are earning, but too few are owning and deciding,” she observed. To address these challenges, the Minister highlighted the importance of business networks that connect women entrepreneurs to mentorship, professional advice, contacts and economic opportunities. She cited a study in Ghana in which growth-oriented women business owners were placed in carefully selected WhatsApp peer groups for 16 weeks. The study found that the participating business owners recorded a 21 per cent increase in their monthly profits, demonstrating the potential of peer networks to improve business performance. The forum also examined practical approaches to creating a more enabling environment for women entrepreneurs, including improved access to finance, technology and markets, as well as stronger business networks. Dr Lartey’s participation reinforced Ghana’s position on the need to move beyond policy commitments towards practical interventions that enable women to grow their enterprises, access wider markets and exercise greater control over their economic opportunities.

items.title: 5 ways smoking can damage your fertility
items.description: Smoking damages male fertility through multiple physiological mechanisms that impair sperm quality, sexual performance, and genetic integrity. If you and your partner are trying to conceive, there are lots of things to help your chances. If you’re a cigarette smoker, quitting the habit is one of them. Here’s what you need to know about smoking and male fertility. 1. Reduced Sperm Count and Concentration Tobacco smoke lowers overall sperm production and semen volume. Studies show that men who smoke have an average reduction in sperm concentration of about 20% to 23% compared to non-smokers, with heavier daily cigarette use leading to a more severe drop. Cigarette smoking reduces sperm quality, giving you a lower sperm count, less semen, and poorer sperm movement. The more cigarettes you smoke, the worse your sperm quality is, but even ‘light’ smokers (less than 10 cigarettes a day) have reduced sperm quality. Smoking can cause DNA damage in sperm, which is linked to an increased risk of miscarriage. 2. Impaired Sperm Motility (Movement) For natural fertilization to happen, sperm must swim effectively through the female reproductive tract. Toxins in cigarette smoke—such as nicotine and heavy metals like cadmium—damage sperm movement, meaning fewer sperm can travel far enough or fast enough to reach the egg. 3. Abnormal Sperm Morphology (Shape) Healthy sperm feature a proper oval-shaped head and a functional tail. Smoking increases the percentage of abnormally shaped sperm such as defects in the head, midpiece, or tail which reduces their ability to attach to and fertilize an egg. 4. Sperm DNA Damage and Oxidative Stress Chemicals in tobacco smoke trigger high levels of oxidative stress, creating harmful reactive oxygen species that overwhelm natural antioxidant defenses. This leads to sperm DNA fragmentation (breaks in the genetic material), which is linked to poorer embryo development and a higher risk of miscarriage. 5. Erectile Dysfunction and Blood Vessel Damage Achieving an erection requires healthy blood flow into the penis. Tobacco smoke damages blood vessels and impairs circulation throughout the body, strongly increasing the risk of erectile dysfunction and making natural conception much more difficult. Erectile dysfunction does not cause infertility, but it can make it harder for you to conceive. And the more you smoke, the higher your risk of erectile dysfunction . To get an erection strong enough for sexual activity, extra blood needs to flow into the penis. Smoking cigarettes damages your blood vessels, which affects blood flow everywhere in the body, including your genitals. In women undergoing IVF treatment, exposure to second-hand smoke may also lead to a reduced chance of successful implantation. Second-hand smoke can also increase the risk of your child being born early and having birth defects. Other ways smoking affects your family Fathers who smoke heavily at the time of conception significantly increase their child’s risk of developing childhood leukaemia. Continuing to smoke around your kids and exposing them to second-hand smoke increases their risk of sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS), asthma, acute chest infections, middle ear disease, conduct problems and learning difficulties. When do you need to quit smoking? Anyone who smokes should stop as soon as possible to enjoy the range of benefits that come with quitting — within two to 12 weeks, your lungs work better, and within one year, your risk of coronary heart disease is half of a smoker’s. However, if your focus is on improving fertility and protecting the health of your future family, quit at least three months before trying for a baby because this is around how long it takes to make new sperm.

items.title: Health Ministry rejects claims of abandoning newly qualified doctors
items.description: The Ministry of Health has dismissed claims that Ghana is training medical doctors and subsequently abandoning them due to delays in recruitment and employment, insisting that established arrangements are in place to facilitate their transition from housemanship into permanent service. In a statement signed by its Spokesperson, Tony Goodman, Esq., on November 5, the Ministry said claims circulating on social media did not accurately represent the processes governing the training, recruitment and employment of newly qualified medical doctors and dentists. While acknowledging the importance of public scrutiny, the Ministry said discussions about its activities must be based on accurate information, stressing that “such discussions must be grounded in facts and a proper understanding of the processes involved”. It explained that the recruitment and posting of house officers were jointly undertaken by the Medical and Dental Council of Ghana and the Ministry of Health. The Ministry disclosed that three batches of medical doctors had commenced housemanship at different periods in 2026, depending on their graduation dates and the completion of the necessary processes. It rejected suggestions that newly qualified doctors were left at home for years awaiting placement, insisting that the existing arrangements allowed them to begin their mandatory practical training after completing the required processes. Housemanship, according to the Ministry, is a structured two-year mandatory programme designed to provide newly qualified doctors and dentists with practical experience at different levels of healthcare delivery. The first year is spent at secondary and tertiary healthcare facilities, while the second year provides trainees with exposure to district-level healthcare delivery. The Ministry said the two years constitute a continuous training programme intended to equip doctors with the clinical experience required before they enter permanent employment. On the financial arrangements, it clarified that clearance covering the entire two-year housemanship programme is obtained before the first year begins, eliminating the need for separate financial approval for progression into the second year. “Consequently, there is no requirement for a separate financial clearance for doctors to progress from the first year to the second year of housemanship,” the statement said. Regarding permanent employment, the Ministry said it had an established arrangement with the Ministry of Finance to facilitate the immediate recruitment of doctors and dentists after their second year of housemanship. “This approach is intended to ensure a smooth transition from mandatory service into permanent employment without unnecessary delays,” it stated. The Ministry disclosed that it was currently recruiting the 36th Batch of Medical Officers and Dentists and preparing to begin the recruitment process for the 37th Batch, whose members had recently obtained permanent registration from the Medical and Dental Council of Ghana. It said the ongoing recruitment exercises demonstrated that procedures were in place to manage the entry of newly qualified medical practitioners into the country’s health workforce. The Ministry also highlighted changes to its recruitment system, explaining that actual vacancies across health facilities were now identified before recruitment exercises commenced. Working with its relevant agencies, it assesses staffing gaps and declares available positions for qualified and eligible doctors and dentists to apply. It said the approach ensures that recruitment and placement are based on identified vacancies and approved staffing requirements rather than indiscriminate postings without consideration of the needs of individual health facilities. The Ministry said the system was intended to promote transparency, accountability and the equitable distribution of medical personnel across the country. It also defended the regulatory framework governing medical education and housemanship, explaining that admission into medical schools was subject to regulatory and accreditation requirements enforced by the Medical and Dental Council of Ghana. The Council, it added, oversees the registration, accreditation and regulation of medical and dental practitioners, including housemanship. The Ministry consequently described suggestions that medical training was unregulated or that the housemanship programme was disorganised as misleading. “Any suggestion that medical training is unregulated or that the housemanship programme is disorganised is misleading and does not reflect the regulatory framework governing medical education and professional practice in Ghana,” it stated. On its broader responsibility to medical professionals, the Ministry acknowledged that training doctors must be accompanied by opportunities for them to serve the country, particularly in underserved and deprived communities. “The Ministry remains committed to ensuring that qualified doctors and dentists are given opportunities to contribute to healthcare delivery, particularly in underserved and deprived communities where their services are most needed,” the statement said. It noted that achieving this required sustainable arrangements for training, recruitment, equitable distribution, deployment and retention of medical professionals. The Ministry said it would continue working with the Ministry of Finance, the Medical and Dental Council, relevant agencies and other stakeholders to strengthen the processes and ensure that Ghana’s investment in medical education translated into improved healthcare delivery. The service urged the public and media practitioners to examine the facts before concluding the recruitment of newly qualified doctors, adding that constructive criticism was welcome when informed by accurate information and an understanding of the relevant processes.

items.title: Tinubu arrives in Akwa Ibom to inaugurate projects, attend APC rally
items.description: President Bola Tinubu has arrived in Uyo, the Akwa Ibom State capital, for a working visit to inaugurate projects executed by Governor Umo Eno’s administration and participate in an All Progressives Congress rally. Tinubu arrived in the state on Friday as part of a two-state visit to Akwa Ibom and Rivers, marking his first major outing in the South-South since the APC began mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. The President was welcomed at Victor Attah International Airport by Eno, government officials, APC leaders and a large crowd of supporters. During the visit, Tinubu is expected to inaugurate several projects at the airport, including its new international terminal building, the International Airport Hospital and the Ibom Aviation Village. He will also inaugurate the Airport-Okopedi Road, linking communities in Nsit Atai and Okobo Local Government Areas, and Ring Road 3, which connects Idoro Road to Ikot Ekpene Road through Uyo and Ibiono Ibom. Other projects scheduled for inauguration include the AKWA-GIS Office Complex, the Command and Control Centre and the ARISE Palm Resort. items.title: Sahara : Staffan de Mistura maintenu en fonction
items.description: L'Organisation des Nations unies a confirmé le maintien de Staffan de Mistura dans ses fonctions d'Envoyé personnel du Secrétaire général pour le Sahara, en dépit des récents développements marqués par le non-renouvellement du mandat de la Minurso et l'amorce de la liquidation de ses opérations. L'avenir à plus long terme de la mission du Suédois reste toutefois tributaire des choix que posera la prochaine hiérarchie onusienne concernant les nominations aux postes de responsabilité supérieure. Lors d'un point de presse tenu jeudi soir, le porte-parole du Secrétaire général des Nations unies, Stéphane Dujarric, a précisé que De Mistura poursuit ses activités depuis son bureau à Bruxelles. Il a rappelé que l'Envoyé personnel a été désigné directement par le Secrétaire général et continue, à ce titre, d'exercer son mandat. Cette mise au point intervient en réponse aux interrogations de la presse quant au rôle exact dévolu au diplomate italo-suédois dans la séquence actuelle, alors que sa mission porte essentiellement sur le volet politique du dossier tandis que la mission d'observation du cessez-le-feu entame sa fermeture. Les échanges ont également porté sur la pertinence de maintenir ce poste et sur une éventuelle fin de mission alignée sur le départ du Secrétaire général sortant. En réaction, Stéphane Dujarric a réitéré l'engagement de l'Organisation à accompagner les parties prenantes dans leurs efforts pour parvenir à une solution politique mutuellement acceptable, si elles en expriment la volonté. Le porte-parole s'est toutefois gardé de donner des garanties sur le maintien de De Mistura à long terme, soulignant que l'identité du futur Secrétaire général n'est pas encore arrêtée et que les décisions relatives aux hauts postes dépendront des orientations de la future gouvernance de l'ONU. The post Sahara : Staffan de Mistura maintenu en fonction appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Manéah : des travailleurs de Topaz manifestent pour réclamer deux mois de salaires impayés
items.description: La colère est montée d’un cran dans la matinée de ce vendredi à Manéah, où plus de 2 500 travailleurs de la société Topaz ont manifesté dans l’enceinte de leur entreprise pour réclamer le paiement de deux mois d’arriérés de salaires. Mis en congé technique depuis deux mois, à la suite de la décision du gouvernement de suspendre la production des sachets en plastiques, ces employés dénoncent une situation devenue de plus en plus difficile pour eux et leurs familles. Munis de pancartes et scandant des slogans réclamant le paiement immédiat de leurs droits, les manifestants ont bloqué l’entrée de l’entreprise afin de faire entendre leurs revendications. À travers cette mobilisation, ils entendent interpeller aussi bien les autorités que la direction de Topaz sur leurs conditions de vie, fortement affectées par cette période prolongée sans rémunération. « Nous sommes en congé technique depuis deux mois, mais jusqu’à présent, nous n’avons reçu aucun salaire. Nous avons des familles à nourrir, des loyers à payer et des enfants à scolariser. Nous demandons simplement le paiement de nos deux mois d’arriérés. Nous ne réclamons rien d’autre que nos droits », a confié Mohamed, l’un des manifestants. Un autre travailleur, visiblement préoccupé par la situation, interpelle directement les autorités : « cette décision a plongé des milliers de travailleurs dans une situation très difficile. Nous comprenons les mesures prises par le gouvernement, mais nous ne devons pas être abandonnés. Nous demandons aux autorités et aux responsables de l’entreprise de trouver rapidement une solution pour nous permettre de rentrer en possession de nos salaires. » Face à cette mobilisation, les responsables communaux de Manéah ont reçu une délégation des manifestants. Les échanges ont permis de calmer les esprits. Les autorités communales ont, à cette occasion, promis de s'impliquer afin de contribuer à trouver une issue favorable à la situation dans les meilleurs délais. En attendant des mesures concrètes, les travailleurs de Topaz restent dans l'expectative. Au-delà de leurs revendications salariales, cette situation met en lumière les conséquences sociales de l'arrêt de la production des sachets plastiques, qui fragilise des milliers de travailleurs et leurs familles.

items.title: Tour du Faso 2026: Paul Daumont prend le maillot jaune à la 8e étape
items.description: Le cycliste burkinabè Paul Daumont a pris, ce vendredi 6 novembre 2026, le maillot jaune, à l’issue de la course de la 8 e étape de la 37 e édition du Tour du Faso, courue entre Ouagadougou-Koupela. La 8 e édition du Tour du Faso a été courue, ce vendredi 6 novembre 2026, entre Ouagadougou et Koupela sur une distance de 153,05 km, repartie en 3 sprints intermédiaires. Au total, ce sont 69 coureurs qui étaient au départ de cette étape. Le premier point chaud à Koulbila (60,57 Km) a été remporté par l’Algérien Anes Riahi qui a été suivi par le Marocain Youssef Bdadou (2 e ) et le Sud Africain Emile Van Nierkerk arrivé 3 e . Le 2 e point chaud à Mogtedo d’une distance de 98,51 Km a vu Riahi franchir en premier la ligne, en 2 e position Bdadou et la 3 e place est occupée par Jannes Van Weele des Pays Bas. L’Algérien Anes Riahi vient encore en première position au 3e point chaud à Zorgho, long de 122,01 Km. Il est toujours suivi par Youssef Bdadou et le Burkinabè Paul Daumont en 3 e position. Cette 8 e étape a été remportée par l’Algérien Anes Riahi. Quant au maillot jaune, il est désormais sur les épaules du Burkinabè Paul Daumont qui a terminé la course troisième qui était détenu par le Sud-Africain Gustav Basson. L’étape a enregistré un abandon. Il s’agit de l’Algérien Hamza Yacine qui a remporté trois étapes du Tour. Il a été victime d’une chute hier à Pô. items.title: Tinubu’s visit: Bus conveying women to welcome president involved in accident
items.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi Several people have sustained injuries on Wednesday after an Akwa Ibom State Transport Corporation (AKTC) bus conveying women to welcome President Bola Tinubu collided with a security vehicle along Oron Road, Uyo. The victims were reportedly among supporters mobilised to join Governor Umo Eno in welcoming the President, who arrived in Akwa Ibom State through Calabar for an official visit. The accident involved the bus, loaded with women heading towards the airport, and a security Hilux van with both vehicles were badly damaged in the collision, leaving several occupants injured and requiring emergency assistance. Nsikakabasi Akpan, who captured the aftermath of the accident, shared footage showing early responders and other persons struggling to evacuate injured victims from the wreckage of the vehicles. He described the incident as an accident along Oron Road involving a bus conveying women to the airport to receive the President and a security Hilux vehicle. Confirming the incident, Paul James, Public Relations Officer, Road Safety Operations, Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Akwa Ibom State Command, said the command had dispatched a response team to the scene. James, however, said the command was yet to establish the extent of casualties and the circumstances surrounding the collision. The reported accident cast a shadow over the build-up to Tinubu’s visit, which attracted supporters and political stakeholders who had gathered to receive the President and his wife, Senator Oluremi Tinubu. The presidential couple were subsequently received by Governor Eno at the Victor Attah International Airport, Uyo, marking the commencement of their engagements in the state. The President’s official visit featured the unveiling of the airport’s new terminal, a major aviation infrastructure project expected to facilitate the commencement of international flight operations from the Victor Attah International Airport. The circumstances surrounding the crash, including the feared death and number of injured victims, were yet to be officially established by the FRSC as of the time of filing this report. items.title: How China's clean-tech machine is reshaping the global climate fight
items.description: China sent $132 billion in clean technology and investment to the developing world last year, by far the largest contribution to carbon-dioxide reduction of any country. In fact, the nation’s green-manufacturing juggernaut, built in part through heavy subsidies from Beijing, nearly matches the current total of grants, loans and private finance that all wealthy countries sent to poorer ones in 2024 to help fight climate change, according to a Reuters analysis. Those loans and grants stemmed from a climate-finance programme the world’s wealthiest nations agreed to at a 2009 United Nations climate conference on the premise that industrialised nations made outsized contributions to the climate crisis — and had outsized means to help poorer countries pay to clean it up. A Reuters investigation in 2024 found that most global climate finance comes in the form of loans and sometimes at market interest rates that funnel billions of dollars back to rich countries. China took a different approach, funneling billions in subsidies into its own green-energy industries , serving its own national interest to dominate next-generation manufacturing domestically and globally. The result: massive and rapid market-share gains in solar panels, batteries and battery minerals, electric vehicles, wind turbines and other green products. China remains by far the world’s biggest greenhouse-gas emitter because of its large population, concentration of heavy industry and reliance on coal power. But its huge clean tech exports mean it has also become among the biggest global forces in reducing climate-damaging emissions. The Reuters analysis used customs data to calculate the value of Chinese exports of clean technologies to countries classified by the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development as developing nations. Those exports alone will help the Global South avoid 257 million metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions (MtCO2) per year once deployed an amount equal to the annual carbon dioxide emissions of France, according to analysis by Lauri Myllyvirta, co-founder of the Helsinki-based Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air. This year’s exports from China, meanwhile, are on track to avoid 337 MtCO2 in the Global South, the analysis shows. Reuters was unable to find a reliable single estimate of how much greenhouse gas emissions are avoided as a result of global climate finance from rich to poor countries. The OECD estimates a fifth of all rich world climate giving in 2024 came from the private sector. The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change and the High Ambition Coalition — an informal coalition of nations that has advocated for substantial climate finance — did not immediately comment for this story. The $132bn figure derived by Reuters for China’s global climate contribution also includes an estimated $40 billion of Chinese foreign direct investment into clean-technology projects in developing countries. The investment data was compiled by Mathias Larsen and Xiaokang Xue at the London School of Economics. That brings China’s contribution to nearly equal to the $137bn in climate finance that wealthy nations provided to poorer ones in 2024 under their UN climate pledges, according to the most recent figures provided by the OECD. The figures are not directly comparable. China’s total largely reflects commercial transactions focused on clean energy development, while climate finance can also support other types of programs like developing climate-resilient agricultural techniques or cleaning up damage from major storms or floods. But the comparison illustrates the extraordinary scale at which China’s manufacturing economy is now shaping the energy transition in poorer countries. The findings point to a potential shift in the mechanics of the global energy transition, according to Li Shuo, a veteran observer of China at UN climate talks who heads the China Climate Hub at the Asia Society Policy Institute. For years, climate talks focused on how much money and technology wealthy countries would provide to poorer ones to help them decarbonise. China’s manufacturing boom is creating another pathway: driving down the price of clean technology through self-interested innovation and scale until developing countries adopt it for economic reasons. “You can align it to your economic agenda,” he said. Export giant, diplomatic mouse Beijing has so far shown little interest in translating its commercial might into diplomatic leadership at global climate talks since President Donald Trump withdrew the United States from international climate cooperation in 2025. China’s diplomatic role likely will take centre stage as nations gather this month for the UN’s COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkiye. Bilateral agreements between heavyweights Washington and Beijing have traditionally paved the way for international climate agreements, including the landmark 2015 Paris deal to limit global warming. But Beijing may be unwilling to go on alone without its geopolitical counterweight at the table, according to former climate negotiators. Beijing may also be worried that taking a bold stance on global carbon reduction would bring unwanted pressure for China to give more climate aid or cut its own fossil-fuel emissions, observers say. China emits about a third of all carbon dioxide emissions and still burns coal for more than half its power. “How China engages on different levels in the coming years is the most fundamental thing that is going to happen on climate because of both their role in clean-tech deployment but also because of their emissions profile,” said Jennifer Morgan, Germany’s former climate minister. China’s Ministry of Commerce said the country is an important contributor to the global green transformation, and that its wind and solar exports have cumulatively reduced global emissions by roughly 4.1bn tonnes of CO2 over the past five years — the equivalent of around 80 per cent of the total emissions of the United States in one year. “Against the backdrop of a global climate governance ‘action deficit’, China will continue to uphold a responsible attitude, working with other countries to address challenges, overcome difficulties, and jointly promote global green and low-carbon transformation and sustainable development,” it said. Forcing out fossil fuels Meanwhile, China’s manufacturing boom has made renewable energy more affordable in the developing world. When Ethiopia banned combustion engine car imports in 2024, for example, it was the first country to take such a dramatic step toward electric vehicles. The decision was less about emissions and more about cutting its fuel import bill, its deputy minister of transport at the time told Reuters . “No one in Ethiopia is asking COP to pay for any of this; the economics have just switched. It is just the cheapest and best solution,” said Larsen, a senior policy fellow at the London School of Economics, who built the database of Chinese green investment used by Reuters in this story. China has been by far the world’s biggest supplier of electric vehicles over the past few years, as dozens of subsidised automakers have waged a fierce price war in China and dramatically increased exports. The green transition has been similarly pragmatic in Pakistan , which imported 17GW worth of solar from China last year, according to data from Ember, roughly on par with Germany’s installations that year. Those panels will cut emissions and, more importantly, provide cheap, reliable power in a country that often has neither. Nearly two thirds of China’s exports of solar panels, and the cells needed to make them, went to the developing world last year, according to Reuters analysis of customs data. The picture is different in wealthy countries like the US and parts of Europe, which in recent years have imposed tariffs and other restrictions on Chinese clean technology to protect their domestic manufacturers from the surge in shipments. The US, for example, imposes tariffs exceeding 100pc on Chinese electric vehicles and has taken other measures to effectively block them from the market. “What is striking is that policies originally designed to address climate change are now facing opposition not because of their climate impacts, but because of concerns about trade and competitiveness,” said Andr Corra do Lago, a veteran climate negotiator for Brazil, which hosted last years climate summit.

items.title: GES extends Obuasi SHTS sexual misconduct probe by 7 days
items.description: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has granted its committee investigating allegations of sexual misconduct involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), Zakaria Abdulai, a seven-day extension to complete its investigations. GES Public Relations Officer, Daniel Fenyi, said the committee had already engaged several people connected to the incident, including some of the alleged victims, but required additional time to ensure their experiences were adequately captured in its report. Speaking on Joy FM’s Midday News, Mr Fenyi explained that the committee was initially given two weeks to complete its work, with the deadline expiring on Wednesday. However, the committee subsequently requested an additional seven days to enable it to engage all the victims identified in the video at the centre of the controversy. He said the investigators were keen to ensure that the final report reflected the actual experiences of the alleged victims rather than being completed without their full representation. The GES PRO expressed the expectation that the committee would reach all the victims by November 11 and submit its report to the GES Council. Mr Fenyi stressed that investigations were still ongoing and dismissed suggestions that the Service had cleared Mr Abdulai or any other individual implicated in the allegations. He emphasised that the GES had not concluded its investigations and that no final determination had been made as of Friday, November 6.

items.title: 37e Tour du Faso/8e étape : Paul Daumont s’empare du maillot jaune à Koupèla
items.description: L'Algérien Anes Riahi a remporté la 8e étape du 37e Tour du Faso courue entre Ouagadougou et Koupèla le vendredi 6 novembre 2026. Longue de 152,64 km la distance a été couverte en 3h23'54 » avec une vitesse moyenne de 44,916 km/h. Paul Daumont du Burkina Faso, 3e à l'arrivée s’empare du maillot jaune de leader. Très attendu, Paul Daumont, vainqueur de l'édition 2025 remet la main sur la tunique de leader à deux étapes du terme. Le Burkinabè parti dans une échappée avec trois autres coureurs à une trentaine de km de l'arrivée a réussi à déjoué la vigilance du porteur du maillot jaune pour la lui arracher à Koupèla grâce à sa 3e place sur le podium du jour. La victoire est revenue à l'Algérien Anes Riahi qui signe le 5e succès d'étape de l'Algérie. Le Marocain Youssef Bdadou est arrivé (2e). Après l'abandon de Yacine Hamza pour cause de blessure, ils étaient 69 au départ de cette 8e étape. Le premier point chaud à Koulbila a été enlevé par l'Algérien Anes Riahi suivi du Marocain Youssef Bdadou et de Emile Van Niekerk de l'Afrique du Sud. Le cycliste algérien va comme la veille s'adjuger les deux autres sprints intermédiaires à Mogtédo puis à Zogho avant de s'imposer sur la ligne finale. Au classement général, hormis le jaune, le maillot vert change d'épaules et est désormais porté par Youssef Bdadou qui garde le maillot des points chauds. Le Burkinabè Soumaïla Ilboudo conserve la tunique du meilleur jeune. Voro KORAHIRE

items.title: Civil Society Call for Scrutiny of United States’ Rights Record
items.description: Click to expand Image Palais des Nations in Geneva, Switzerland, June 16, 2025. © 2025 Lian Yi/Xinhua via Getty Images The United States is scheduled to appear in Geneva on November 10 for its Universal Periodic Review, the United Nations’ peer review process of every member state’s rights record. But the US is unlikely to show: the Trump administration declared in 2025 that the US would not participate. After the US failed to turn up in November 2025, the review was rescheduled. Should the US again fail to appear next week, it should not be given another extension and should not be exempt from this process which, as the name suggests, applies to every UN member country. As part of the process, US and international rights groups, including Human Rights Watch, made 192 submissions highlighting a range of human rights issues. The civil society submissions paint a worrying picture, with a dramatic worsening of the US government’s rights record over the past year. At President Trump’s direction, the US government dismantled its civil rights enforcement apparatus. It has also violated the prohibition on non-refoulement and sent Venezuelan men to torture in El Salvador’s prisons. The Trump administration also continues to retaliate against opponents, restrict the rights of transgender people, and eliminate regulations that curb climate warming pollutants, among other things. In an unprecedented assault on the rule of law, the administration escalated its sanctions against the ICC, targeting the court as a whole. State legislation and targeted federal funding cuts have dramatically reduced access to safe abortion care and other reproductive health care in many states, curtailing women’s rights. During the immigration crackdown, authorities have separated breastfeeding and other parents from their children and have detained pregnant women despite a longstanding government policy that directs agencies to avoid this except in limited circumstances. The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights has highlighted concerns about deaths in immigration detention; harmful migration policies and enforcement; and sanctions against the ICC and Palestinian rights groups. The UN Special Procedures mandate holders have also raised concerns regarding: unlawful killings at sea; allegedly arbitrary removal of immigration judges and politicization of immigration courts; and unlawful use of lethal force by immigration enforcement agents. The US government is attempting to dodge international scrutiny of these serious and well-documented abuses. The Human Rights Council should not let that happen. This is a time for greater rights scrutiny in the US, not less.
