items.title: Makkah Defence Alliance secretary general to assume duties in Riyadh soon: FO
items.description: The Foreign Office (FO) on Friday said that the secretary general of the Makkah Defence Alliance, retired Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood, is expected to assume his responsibilities in Riyadh soon. Mahmood was appointed on Sep 23 as the first secretary general of the alliance between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, signed on Aug 7, empowers the three members to consider an armed attack on one member an attack on all. Speaking at the FO’s weekly press briefing on Friday, Spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan further said that the three members would jointly decide on convening a meeting of their alliance. The Makkah Defence Alliance has garnered particular attention as Saudi Arabia faces attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels, including a deadly strike that closed Riyadh’s international airport for two weeks last month. Pakistan is providing “whatever support is needed” to defend Saudi Arabia amid the Houthi attacks, the military’s spokesperson Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said in mid-October. However, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) director general also clarified that all members of the Makkah Defence Alliance were “absolutely clear […] that this alliance has no offensive intent; it is purely defensive”. The DG ISPR added: “Pakistan is giving very strong signals that this collective deterrence is at play, has already been actualised and we will take all necessary steps for the security and territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the Haramain Sharifain (The Two Holy Mosques).” Islamabad has two defence pacts with Riyadh aimed at collective deterrence — the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement between the two and the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement that also includes Turkiye. On Thursday, the Turkish parliament approved a bill ratifying the Makkah pact , paving the way for the trilateral security pact to come into force. On its part, FO said late last month that Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already completed the ratification processes, noting that each country followed its own constitutional and legal procedures to approve and ratify international agreements. Pakistan, others actively making efforts for peace in Middle East In his briefing, Khan also touched upon the crisis in the Gulf, saying that Pakistan would continue its efforts to facilitate dialogue in the conflict involving Iran and the United States. He said Islamabad had brought the two parties under one roof despite them having remained out of contact for decades and supported a peaceful resolution through dialogue and diplomacy. Khan cited the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between the warring parties on June 18 as “proof” of Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts. He added that Pakistan, Qatar and other countries were actively contributing to mediation efforts. The FO official emphasised that peace in the region could be established through “political dialogue and diplomacy” rather than war. While acknowledging that the process of negotiations could be time-consuming, Khan asserted that issues could be resolved via diplomacy. Elaborating further, the FO spokesperson said Israel was playing the role of a “spoiler” in the ongoing US-Iran war. Criticising Israel’s expansionist policies, he said peace in the region was not in Israel’s interest and that its expansionist ambitions were among the major causes of the current regional crisis. These ambitions were not limited to Iran, he said, adding that Palestine, Syria, Lebanon and other countries in the region were also affected by Israel’s expansionist designs. When asked about the recent midterm elections in the US, the FO spokesperson said elections were an internal matter of that country and reiterated that Pakistan maintained close relations with Washington. Democrats seized control of the US Congress earlier this week, capturing the Senate and House of Representatives in a stunning, nationwide rejection of Donald Trump set to put the brakes on the final two years of his presidency.

items.title: Nine parties back ADC after David Mark’s leadership sack
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Nine opposition parties under the Coalition for Democracy have rallied behind the African Democratic Congress ADC, describing Thursday’s Federal High Court judgment which dissolved the Senator David Mark-led leadership of the party and invalidate its presidential candidacy as “a dangerous escalation in what appears to be a systematic campaign to eliminate credible political opposition ahead of the 2027 general elections.” In a statement signed by Salihu Moh. Lukman, on behalf of the coalition parties, the group warned that what is happening to the ADC today can happen to every opposition party tomorrow. The Coalition for Democracy emerged from the G100 Opposition Summit held in Abuja on 31 August 2026. Its members are the ADC, Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Democratic Leadership Alliance (DLA), National Rescue Movement (NRM), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Social Democratic Party (SDP) and Youth Progressives Party (YPP). The platform describes itself as committed to defending Nigeria’s constitutional democracy, protecting political pluralism and ensuring free, fair, credible and competitive elections. The Coalition recalled that it had only a day earlier raised the alarm over Nigeria’s shrinking democratic space, citing attacks on opposition supporters, obstruction of political activities and “the increasing weaponisation of state institutions against political competitors.” “When opposition parties are attacked on the streets, frustrated by state institutions, and threatened with elimination through judicial pronouncements, Nigerians must ask whether the ruling party still intends to face any meaningful opposition at the ballot box,” the statement said. The Coalition said it respects the independence of the judiciary and the right of aggrieved parties to seek legal redress, but insisted that “the courts must never become instruments through which political competition is extinguished. “Those who seek to destroy the opposition in order to guarantee their own victory must understand that they are not merely threatening political parties; they are threatening the very foundations of the Republic. A government that cannot tolerate opposition has lost the moral authority to call itself democratic. “When a government becomes more afraid of the opposition than it is accountable to the people, democracy itself is in danger”, the parties added. It warned that the narrowing of democratic space “carries grave consequences for national stability,” adding: “No democracy can remain peaceful when citizens are denied meaningful political alternatives. “The ballot must remain the battlefield of democracy. No political party should be allowed to achieve through institutional manipulation what it fears it cannot achieve through the votes of Nigerians,” it said. The Coalition declared its solidarity with the ADC in its decision to challenge the judgment through the appropriate judicial processes. It called on all opposition parties, civil society organisations, the Nigerian Bar Association, organised labour, the media and patriotic Nigerians “to unite in peaceful, lawful resistance against every attempt to undermine political pluralism. “Let it be known: the Coalition for Democracy will not stand by while Nigeria is reduced to a democracy without opposition, elections without alternatives, and ballots without genuine choices. An attack on one is an attack on all. We will resist it together”, the parties declared. Vanguard News The post Nine parties back ADC after David Mark’s leadership sack appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Imaan, Hadi move IHC against conviction in security breach case
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her spouse Hadi Ali Chattha on Friday filed appeals in the Islamabad High Court (IHC) against their convictions by an anti-terrorism court in the security breach case. They also moved applications seeking the suspension of their sentences and release on bail pending appeal. The appeals were filed by advocates Faisal Siddiqui, Riasat Ali Azad and Zainab Janjua under Section 25 of the Anti-Terrorism Act read with Section 410 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) against the court’s order. On Oct 29, an ATC sentenced Imaan and Hadi to 10 years in prison each in the security breach case. The court also handed down one-year sentences and imposed fines of Rs50,000 each under Section 186 (obstructing a public servant in the discharge of public functions) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC). They were also sentenced to two years each under Section 353 (assault or criminal force to deter a public servant from discharging his duty) of the PPC. In the identical appeals, the counsel contended that the trial court failed to meet the requirements of a fair trial and that the conviction was the result of patently illegal and arbitrary proceedings. It was argued that the charge was framed without providing copies under Section 265-C CrPC and that a plea of “not guilty” was recorded on the appellants’ behalf although none was taken. They further submitted that the prosecution evidence was recorded in the absence of the appellants and their counsel, contrary to Section 353 CrPC and Article 10-A of the Constitution. The appeal also challenged the jail trial, arguing that it was conducted in a manner akin to a secret trial and without lawful authority, and that the appellants were not allowed a proper and confidential consultation with their counsel. It further contended that state counsel was imposed on the appellants against their stated wishes and that the trial court proceeded with the case despite a transfer application pending before the high court, in violation of Section 526(8) of the CrPC. On the merits, the appeal argued that the conviction under Section 7 of the ATA was unsustainable because the prosecution failed to prove the design or purpose required under Section 6 of the ATA. It said the trial court itself described the incident as “a very common nature, ordinary type of incident” and that the evidence showed the appellants were on their way to court when they were held up at the barrier. The appellants have prayed that the impugned judgment be set aside and that they be acquitted. Meanwhile, in the accompanying suspension applications, their counsel sought suspension of the sentences and release on bail, contending that the conviction was rendered during the pendency of a transfer application and that the bar under Section 25(8) of the ATA was not absolute when read with Section 25(5) of the law. ‘Misuse of criminal justice system’ Separately, over 20 international human rights organisations, including Amnesty International, called on the government to “immediately and unconditionally” release Imaan and Hadi. In a joint statement on Friday, 23 organisations, including Alliance for Lawyers at Risk, Défense Sans Frontière, New York City Bar Association, Council of Bars and Law Societies of Europe, Geneva Bar Association, Lawyers for Lawyers, and PEN Norway, condemned the recent sentences and sought an end to the “extensive misuse” of the criminal justice system against the two lawyers. It said that the convictions raised serious concerns over anti-terrorism legislation being used “to criminally punish and intimidate lawyers undertaking permissible human rights work”. Referring to the case proceedings, the statement noted that the verdict was delivered despite a petition pending in the Supreme Court. “Proceedings in these circumstances raise concerns about respect for due process and the right to an effective judicial remedy,” the organisations said, expressing concern that the trial, which was conducted at the Adiala jail in Rawalpindi, did not meet fair trial standards. The organisations noted that the couple had been kept in a “cage-like” structure in the courtroom throughout the trial, rendering them unable to communicate with their counsel effectively. They also noted that the counsel was not given sufficient access to Imaan and Hadi. “The prosecution relied primarily on police testimony to establish the offence, while the defence were denied adequate opportunity to reasonably challenge prosecutorial evidence,” the statement read, adding that the couple had denied the charges and maintained they were being targeted for their professional work and activism. The organisations raised alarm that the “misuse of overbroad anti-terrorism legislation to the alleged removal of security barriers raises serious questions about the proportionality of the charges”. It observed that such legislation must not be applied “arbitrarily or disproportionately, nor used to intimidate individuals or punish permissible conduct or activities that do not meet the applicable threshold”. The organisations called for the convictions to be seen in the context of “successive, politically motivated, criminal proceedings” against the couple, which were “solely to punish them for and deter them from continuing their peaceful, permissible human rights work”. They also recalled the SC’s September 17 suspension of their 17-year sentences in the social media posts case and subsequent rearrest. “The successive proceedings in the barrier removal case, and their prolonged deprivation of liberty despite the SC’s intervention, reinforce our concern that the criminal proceedings are calculated to make an example of the two lawyers and risk creating a chilling effect on the independence of the legal profession in Pakistan and on access to justice more broadly.” In this regard, the organisations cited Article 10A of the Constitution, which guarantees the right to a fair trial and due process, as well as Pakistan’s status as a party to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR). “Anti-terrorism legislation must not be used to criminalise peaceful assembly, protected expression, freedom of association or permissible professional activity,” the organisations stated. “The arrest, prosecution or prolonged detention of the lawyers because of their professional representation, human rights advocacy and exercise of their right to freedom of expression not only violates their personal human rights – it also sends a stark warning to other legal professionals and human rights defenders.” They noted that such actions had a “wider chilling effect” on the legal profession in the country and undermined lawyers’ ability to represent politically sensitive or human rights cases “without fear of reprisal”. In the joint statement, the 23 organisations called on the government and relevant authorities to “immediately and unconditionally” release Imaan and Hadi and “take appropriate steps to have the convictions against them quashed”. It also called for an end to “misuse of the criminal justice system to target the two lawyers and drop any charges and cases against them arising solely from their work and defence of human rights”. Further, the organisations urged the government to review the use of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act as well as anti-terrorism legislation against lawyers, journalists, human rights defenders, and peaceful critics and comply with Pakistan’s obligations under the ICCPR in terms of domestic laws and their enforcement. “Judicial remedies cannot be meaningful if a grant of liberty by one court is followed immediately by detention through another proceeding without sufficient credible evidence,” it further stated. The organisations expressed solidarity with Imaan and Hadi and “with all lawyers in Pakistan who continue to defend human rights and the rule of law despite the fear of reprisals”. “We call on the Pakistani authorities to respect their international obligations, uphold the independence of the legal profession and ensure that lawyers can exercise their profession and their human rights without intimidation, retaliation or improper interference,” the statement concluded.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and its intended consequences for national security
items.description: The age and era of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has gradually crept up on us. This means there is nothing we can do about it but embrace it. AI has positive and negative effects for organizations, stakeholders, the state, and national security. AI has numerous benefits all over the globe; it has become a tool that is being used for various purposes. AI is used in hospitals for diagnosis, used in classrooms to aid learners, and even used in warfare, predicting enemy lines for counterattack. Advanced countries and institutions have resorted to the use of AI for ease in modern warfare and productivity. Weapons have now been fitted with aspects of AI to ascertain the exact locations of targets. This critical dimension makes artificial intelligence a tool that we in the Global South need to take seriously. When we look at the aspect of misinformation and disinformation, we need not overlook the fact that AI is being used in a negative way. With associated attacks in cyberspace, misinformation and disinformation are very worrying when AI is used. Happenings around the globe with regard to the use of AI have shown that the tool is being used to destroy cryptocurrency investments. Recent narratives have established that financial crimes were committed in the cryptocurrency markets because a worker’s laptop was infected with AI software. This is a very worrying spectacle. We are hearing financial institutions also losing their security space to AI threats. Some banks in Asia have been hacked using AI software, and automated cyber-attacks via AI tools are occurring across the globe. The question then is: what happens with us in the Global South? So, for a country like Ghana, have we fully embraced artificial intelligence? Looking at the threats and challenges in the fight against cyber-attacks, what this means is that criminal elements have become more sophisticated, trying to find loopholes in the security system to be able to outwit the security agencies and managers of the country using AI tools. Arrests have been made regarding Ghanaian citizens alleged to have used AI to create fake images to engage in cyber fraud and romance scams. Our security architecture must embrace this tool as a matter of national security. This will go a long way to assist fight crime and predict crimes and identify the perpetuators. In the end, the tool can have a positive impact on our security landscape when applied efficiently. Africa as a whole needs to really invest in artificial intelligence to understand the intricacies for security purposes, protection, and prevention of crimes and conflict. Otherwise, we’ll be taken by surprise when attacks are targeted against our financial institutions and our security apparatus. We need to learn to use AI. Various institutions in the country need to embrace it for the purposes of protection and prevention of any attacks. We must be mindful of the fact that the impact of AI is too great to leave unmanaged. Strong governance policies and investment in people are what will keep its use safe and effective. Here are some of the key benefits of the use of AI in Cybersecurity: AI in cybersecurity enables real-time threat detection, automated response, and large-scale data analysis to mitigate risks faster than traditional approaches. AI-powered cybersecurity strengthens endpoints, networks, and cloud security through phishing detection, behavioral analytics, vulnerability management, and authentication. AI reduces manual effort and human error while improving efficiency, accelerating response times, and enhancing overall security posture. Effective adoption requires high-quality data, continuous model updates, human in the loop, and integration across the security stack. AI-driven security introduces risks like adversarial AI and data poisoning, requiring adaptive and continuously evolving defense strategies. Over the past few months, we have seen a rise in adversarial AI attacks, data poisoning, AI tools hacking one another, and simulated attacks. Organizations looking to adopt AI should invest in training their people. AI adoption is valuable, but only if organizations invest in AI training, establish governance processes, and continuously evolve their defense strategies. Authors Kwame Asomaning: Technologist & Cybersecurit y Professional Victor Doke, PhD, is a Security Analyst and Lecturer, Ghana Armed Forces Command and Staff College (GAFCSC)

items.title: Igbokoda air crash: NAF recovers cockpit voice recorder
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has recorded further progress in the recovery and investigation of the ATR-42 aircraft accident in Igbokoda, Ondo State, with the recovery of the Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR), confirmed intact by technical teams from the NAF and Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB). Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, Director of Public Relations and Information disclosed this in a statement on Friday. He said, “Part of the Flight Data Recorder (FDR), commonly referred to as the black box, was also retrieved, while efforts to locate and recover its remaining portion continue. “Additional aircraft wreckage, engine components and human remains have also been recovered. “Operations are ongoing in the challenging swamp terrain, with teams working to retrieve outstanding components and facilitate the necessary technical examinations. “The investigation is being conducted with due diligence to ensure comprehensive, evidence-based findings. “The recovery process also involves careful attention to the proper handling of human remains, with the Directorate of Identification and Classification (DIC) undertaking the necessary procedures for proper identification. “The NAF has sustained engagements with the families of the victims, recognising their need for information and support. “Engagement with relevant authorities on environmental concerns raised by the host community also remains an important part of the broader response. “While appreciating the public’s concern and interest, the NAF appeals for continued patience and understanding as these critical processes require time, careful coordination and professional attention. “The ultimate objective is not only to establish the circumstances surrounding the accident but also to draw the necessary lessons to strengthen flight safety, enhance ongoing airpower operations and further safeguard the lives of personnel and citizens. “The NAF remains committed to providing verified updates as appropriate.” The post Igbokoda air crash: NAF recovers cockpit voice recorder appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Port regional de Kaolack : Tous les quais affichent plein
items.description: Le Port régional de Kaolack retrouve progressivement une animation qu’il n’avait plus connue depuis longtemps. En début de semaine, ses trois postes à quai opérationnels affichent complet, avec la présence simultanée de trois navires de 2.500 à 3.000 tonnes, engagés dans des opérations commerciales. Kaolack – Le port de Kaolack reprend des couleurs. Pour la première fois depuis des années, tous ses quais sont occupés. Un signe encourageant de la reprise des activités portuaires. Les navires présents déchargent des marchandises destinées au Mali. À l’issue de ces opérations, ils vont embarquer du sel à destination de plusieurs ports de la sous-région, notamment celui d’Abidjan. Ces rotations s’inscrivent dans le cadre de lignes régulières, avec des escales hebdomadaires à Kaolack. Sur les terre-pleins également, l’activité reprend. Marchandises, engins de manutention et dockers mobilisés donnent au site une véritable physionomie portuaire. Cette dynamique fait suite à plusieurs escales remarquées, notamment celle d’un navire de croisière en provenance des États-Unis, puis du bâtiment de guerre de la Marine nationale, le Fadiouth. Cette reprise ne doit toutefois pas occulter les contraintes liées à la navigation sur le Saloum. Il y a une semaine, un navire s’est échoué près de Lyndiane, à environ cinq kilomètres du port. Un incident qui rappelle l’urgence du dragage de la voie navigable, indispensable pour sécuriser la navigation et permettre l’accueil de navires de 5.000 à 7.000 tonnes. Pour Abdoulaye Sogue, responsable du Port régional de Kaolack, relevant du Port autonome de Dakar (Pad), cette opération devrait figurer parmi les priorités du programme d’investissements prévu dans le cadre de la célébration de la fête de l’Indépendance à Kaolack, en 2029. Annoncée par le Président de la République lors du Conseil des ministres du 13 octobre dernier, cette échéance représente une opportunité pour inscrire le dragage du Saloum parmi les projets structurants de la région. Au-delà de cette occupation exceptionnelle des quais, l’enjeu est économique et stratégique. Le Port régional de Kaolack ambitionne de jouer pleinement son rôle de plateforme complémentaire à celle de Dakar, en contribuant à sa décongestion et en offrant une alternative logistique aux opérateurs économiques. Sa position géographique constitue un atout pour capter davantage de trafic à destination du Mali et desservir les régions du centre et de l’est du Sénégal. « Elle confirme que le Port de Kaolack dispose d’une capacité opérationnelle et d’un potentiel de développement qui méritent d’être davantage valorisés au service de l’économie nationale et des échanges sous-régionaux », s’est réjoui Abdoulaye Sogue. Il a également salué les efforts de la nouvelle équipe portuaire et de l’armateur national Csttao. Ancien deuxième port de l’Afrique-Occidentale française (Aof), Kaolack entend renouer avec son prestige commercial. Depuis 2023, ses infrastructures portuaires sont gérées par le Port autonome de Dakar, dirigé par Doune Pathé Mbengue. Une intégration qui ouvre de nouvelles perspectives, à condition de consentir les investissements nécessaires, notamment le dragage du Saloum. Mamadou THIAM (Correspondant)

Abdoulaye Diop à RT en français : contrer la désinformation, un enjeu important pour la Russie et le Mali
items.description: En marge du Salon des medias du Mali, qui se tient du 5 au 8 novembre a Bamako, le ministre malien des Affaires etrangeres, Abdoulaye Diop, a confie, dans un entretien exclusif au micro de RT, sa vision de la collaboration et du partenariat avec le media, percu comme une « alliance strategique entre nos differents pays, notamment la Confederation des etats du Sahel et la Federation de Russie », dans la lutte contre la desinformation. Le chef de la diplomatie malienne a d'emblee souligne les diverses formes de collaboration entre RT en francais et les pays du Sahel, entre promotion de la formation et echange d'experiences. L'« alliance » avec le media s'inscrit dans le sillage de l'alliance gouvernementale entre la Federation de Russie et les pays de l'Alliance des etats du Sahel (AES) pour developper « un autre narratif, porter nos propres recits » et avoir acces a une information « credible, professionnelle et equilibree ». RT incarne une nouvelle dimension du partenariat entre la Russie et le Mali sur le front geopolitique de l'information Abdoulaye Diop a rappele que la collaboration entre la Russie et les pays de l'AES etait surtout axee sur les questions de defense, de securite et d'acces a des equipements militaires dans le cadre de la lutte contre le terrorisme. « Aujourd'hui, la menace sur le terrain s'est transformee », a-t-il souligne, pointant une evolution de la menace qui a glisse sur le terrain de l'information. Selon le chef de la diplomatie malienne, « les medias sont aujourd'hui devenus aussi des armes de destruction massive » dont les derives pourraient « tuer les gens » si elles ne sont pas controlees. Dans ce contexte, il a insiste sur la necessite de bien s'equiper dans cette guerre de l'information, et c'est a ce stade qu'intervient le partenariat avec RT, en tant que media qui « peut nous aider a faire entendre notre voix, a faire en sorte qu'il y ait des voix et des sons alternatifs qui donnent des options aux gens ». RT comme moyen alternatif pour s'informer et « voir le monde » « Aujourd'hui, avec RT et beaucoup d'autres chaînes chinoises ou autres, ca nous donne le choix, ca donne aussi l'acces a une autre facon d'informer, mais aussi, au-dela d'une autre facon d'informer, c'est une autre facon de voir le monde », a declare Abdoulaye Diop, faisant etat d'une convergence des visions de la Russie et des pays de l'AES en matiere d'information, de communication et de diplomatie « peuple a peuple ». Dans ce contexte, le chef de la diplomatie malienne a exprime la conviction que seuls les medias « permettent de faire en sorte que nos populations se renforcent davantage dans cette lutte, que nous puissions nous donner la main et nous renforcer mutuellement la ou il y a des capacites ». Revenant sur les declarations de la directrice de RT en francais, Natalia Lebedeva, lors de son intervention au Salon des medias du Mali, qui a fait savoir que le personnel de RT au Mali etait constitue de Maliens, Abdoulaye Diop a explique qu'il s'agit de « signaux extremement importants pour nous de ne pas remplacer les capacites qui existent dans nos pays, mais de les renforcer et de nous donner la voix », felicitant dans la foulee le soutien du media russe aux pays de la region. Au terme de l'entretien, le ministre malien des Affaires etrangeres a souligne la necessite de s'inspirer et d'apprendre du modele russe dans son investissement et sa comprehension de « la nature strategique de l'information ». « Nos pays aussi devront pouvoir apprendre de l'importance que la Russie donne aujourd'hui a ces elements et voir comment nous pouvons travailler ensemble, parce que, quand on dit une guerre, ca necessite necessairement des moyens, des capacites et une bonne comprehension des cibles que nous cherchons a atteindre », a-t-il conclu. Le Salon des medias du Mali, qui organise actuellement sa cinquieme edition, est un rendez-vous important dans le paysage mediatique malien. Il represente une occasion pour les professionnels des medias locaux et africains d'echanger, de se former et de renforcer leurs capacites autour de conferences-debats sur les enjeux du secteur mediatique, de panels de discussion et de seances de formation professionnelle.

items.title: Hamzat promises 40% funding for youth apprenticeship
items.description: By Henry Ojelu The Lagos State All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship flag bearer for the 2027 election, Dr Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, has promised that his administration will provide 40 per cent funding for stipends of apprentices as part of efforts to equip young people with practical skills and improve their employability. Hamzat made the pledge during an interactive session organised by the Lagos State chapter of the Nigerian Society of Engineers (NSE), where he outlined his plans for youth development, skills acquisition and innovation. He said the proposed funding would encourage businesses to take on apprentices and work with professional bodies to provide young people with relevant vocational and technical training. According to him, emphasis would also be placed on practical skills in artificial intelligence, AI, robotics and other emerging technologies, as well as vocational training and professional certification. Hamzat said the initiative would enable young people to acquire skills and qualifications that would improve their chances of securing jobs and accessing finance. He also pledged to strengthen the capacity of the Lagos State Science, Research and Innovation Council to support young innovators through funding, investment opportunities and global exposure. He said the plan was to create an enabling environment for entrepreneurs to develop, commercialise and scale their innovations, while contributing to the state’s economic growth. The post Hamzat promises 40% funding for youth apprenticeship appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NDC sets November 9 deadline for national executive nominations
items.description: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) will conclude the filing of nominations for its national executive positions on Monday, November 9, as the party advances its 2026 internal electoral process towards the election of new national officers in December. The filing of nominations is scheduled to take place from Saturday, November 7, to Monday, November 9, following the 14-day period allocated to aspirants to complete their nomination forms. According to the party’s electoral timetable, the vetting of national executive aspirants will take place on Thursday, November 12, and Friday, November 13, at the National Secretariat. An appeals process has also been scheduled for Sunday, November 15, and Monday, November 16. The national electoral process will culminate in the party’s National Congress on Saturday, December 19, 2026, where new national executives are expected to be elected. Regional elections scheduled for November 14–15 Ahead of the national congress, the NDC will hold its Regional Youth and Women Conference on Friday, November 13, followed by regional executive elections on Saturday, November 14, and Sunday, November 15. The regional elections form part of the party’s broader internal reorganisation process, which is expected to produce new leadership at the various levels ahead of the 2028 General Elections. National Youth and Women Conference The party has also scheduled its National Youth and Women Conference for Saturday, December 12, although the venue is yet to be announced. The conference will precede the National Congress on December 19, which will mark the culmination of the party’s 2026 internal electoral exercise. Party urges adherence to timetable The NDC has urged all regional and constituency executives, aspirants and members to carefully study the electoral timetable and comply with the stipulated procedures, timelines and deadlines. It said strict adherence to the roadmap was necessary to safeguard the credibility and integrity of the elections and ensure that all stages of the process were conducted fairly and transparently. The party also expressed appreciation to its members, executives and stakeholders for their continued dedication, discipline and commitment to its ideals. It said the unity and collective spirit demonstrated throughout the reorganisation process would strengthen the party as it prepares for the 2028 General Elections.

items.title: 4.8 tonnes of marijuana with over US$1m street value heading towards Nigeria seized by Ghana Navy
items.description: Two large wooden boats carrying 117 sacks of substances suspected to be marijuana, with an estimated street value of more than US$1 million, have been intercepted by the Ghana Navy in an intelligence-led operation on the Volta Lake estuary at Ada in the Greater Accra Region. The operation, conducted by the Riverine Command of the Ghana Navy at about 1 a.m. on Thursday, November 5, prevented the suspected consignment from being transported outside the country via the sea. The boats were discovered concealed along the banks of the river near the estuary. They were in the preparatory stages of transporting the narcotics to Nigeria. They fled the scene and abandoned the boat when they saw Navy personnel approaching. Addressing a press conference on Thursday, the Director of Naval Operations at the Naval Headquarters, Naval Captain Festus Osei-Brobbey, said the suspects abandoned the boats and fled upon sighting the naval patrol team. He said the boats were subsequently moved to Ada Foah, where they were searched at about 5 a.m. in the presence of officials of the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC). The search revealed 117 sacks containing approximately 80 packs of suspected marijuana each, bringing the estimated total weight of the consignment to 4.8 tons. Naval Captain Osei-Brobbey said the substances have been handed over to NACOC to conduct the necessary laboratory examination. He described the seizure as potentially the biggest marijuana interception by the Navy in the recent past, recalling an earlier operation in July during which about 60 sacks of suspected marijuana were intercepted. He said the operation formed part of the Navy’s commitment to combating illicit activities within Ghana’s maritime domain and supporting President John Dramani Mahama’s zero-tolerance stance on drug trafficking. He indicated that the operation also reinforced national efforts to strengthen border security, improve inter-agency cooperation and prevent the use of Ghana as a transit point for illicit substances. Naval Captain Osei-Brobbey warned financiers, sponsors, organisers and other individuals involved in drug trafficking that the Navy would intensify surveillance and monitoring operations to identify, track and disrupt criminal networks operating within the country’s maritime corridors. He said the Navy would continue to work with other security agencies and stakeholders to protect Ghana’s territorial waters against drug trafficking and other illicit activities. He also appealed to the public to provide credible and actionable information to support the security agencies in their operations. He also appealed to the public to provide credible and actionable information to support the security agencies in their operations. Assembly The Municipal Chief Executive (MCE) for Ada East, Kenneth Kofi Kabu Kanor, who also addressed the press conference, expressed concern about the growing challenge of drug abuse and its impact on families and communities. He said the geographical location of Ada, with its river and sea connections, made it important for authorities to strengthen surveillance and prevent the waterways from being exploited for illegal activities. Mr Kanor called for stronger collaboration between the district assembly, security agencies and the central government to tackle drug trafficking and other illegal activities. He further stressed the need to protect the area’s waterways and promote responsible use of its natural resources, saying the fight against illicit trade required collective commitment.

items.title: Ebola en RDC : 5 198 morts recensés et le Ghana en alerte
items.description: En Republique democratique du Congo (RDC), 10 668 cas confirmes d'Ebola et 5 198 deces ont ete recenses au 3 novembre, selon un bilan publie le 5 novembre par le Centre europeen de prevention et de controle des maladies. L'epidemie, causee par le virus Bundibugyo, a touche huit provinces du pays. Sur le terrain, retrouver les personnes exposees au virus reste un obstacle majeur. Africa CDC indique que plus de 85 % des nouveaux malades n'avaient pas ete identifies auparavant comme contacts a surveiller. Pres de deux deces sur trois surviennent en dehors des centres de traitement. L'Ituri, dans le nord-est de la RDC, concentre a elle seule 7 485 infections et 3 532 morts. Les equipes medicales doivent composer avec les groupes armes, les routes difficiles et les fortes pluies. Dans le Nord-Kivu, a l'est du pays, 2 593 infections et 1 422 deces ont ete recenses. Au total, 67 zones de sante sont concernees a travers le pays. La peur de la contamination eloigne aussi des femmes et des enfants des centres de sante . Le Ghana controle les arrivees Au Ghana, les autorites ont renforce des le 3 novembre les controles sanitaires dans les trois aeroports internationaux du pays. Aucun cas d'Ebola n'y a ete confirme. Les passagers doivent renseigner leurs deplacements recents sur un formulaire, puis passer un controle de temperature. Ceux qui presentent des symptomes suspects sont isoles et evalues. Les personnes arrivant de pays ou Ebola circule seront suivies jusqu'a 21 jours. Les hotels devront declarer aux autorites la presence de clients venus des zones touchees et noter les personnes qui leur rendent visite. Mentir sur ses voyages, cacher des symptomes ou refuser le controle sanitaire expose a des sanctions. Le directeur general d'Africa CDC, Jean Kaseya, a reagi le 3 novembre aux restrictions de voyage decidees par le Kenya. « Le monde est plus sûr lorsque les pays cooperent pour mettre fin aux epidemies, plutot que d'isoler les pays touches », a-t-il declare. Deux vaccins a l'essai L'Organisation mondiale de la Sante (OMS) a annonce le 4 novembre que deux nouveaux vaccins pourraient rejoindre l'essai clinique Tumaini, deja en cours en RDC, sous reserve des autorisations nationales necessaires. L'un vient de l'universite d'Oxford, l'autre de Moderna. Aucun vaccin dirige contre cette souche du virus Ebola n'a encore recu d'autorisation de mise sur le marche. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, directeur general de l'OMS, a rappele les limites de la vaccination : « a eux seuls, les vaccins ne suffiront pas pour mettre fin a cette epidemie, mais ils pourraient devenir un nouvel outil puissant pour la maîtriser. »

items.title: Minority demands probe into Akamai shutdown of digital health systems over US$64m debt
items.description: The Minority in Parliament has demanded an investigation into the suspension of critical electronic health information systems in Ghana following an outstanding payment of approximately US$64,511 to technology services provider Akamai. The caucus says the disruption raises serious questions about the government’s financial planning, contract management and oversight of the country’s digital health infrastructure. In a press statement dated November 6, 2026, the Ranking Member of Parliament’s Health Committee, Dr Nana Ayew Afriye, said the Ghana Health Service (GHS) had disclosed in a communication dated November 2 that critical electronic health information systems, including the District Health Information Management System (DHIMS2), had been inaccessible since October 29. The shutdown reportedly followed the suspension of ten servers by Akamai over an outstanding payment of US$64,510.95. The Minority described the development as troubling, particularly against the backdrop of the government’s assurances that the introduction of the Ghana Health Information Management System (GHIMS) would strengthen national control over health data and reduce dependence on private service providers. In October 2025, Health Minister Kwabena Mintah Akandoh announced the introduction of GHIMS to replace the Lightwave Health Information Management System (LHIMS). Although GHIMS and DHIMS2 perform different functions, the Minority says both are part of Ghana’s wider digital health ecosystem, raising concerns about the sustainability of the government’s digital health strategy. The caucus has also questioned the resources committed to the digital health transformation, noting that the Ministry of Health’s budget increased from approximately GH¢17.8 billion in 2025 to GH¢22.8 billion in 2026, representing a 28 per cent nominal increase. It is, however, demanding a detailed account of the specific allocations and expenditure on GHIMS and related digital infrastructure, as well as the measurable outcomes achieved. The Minority further criticised the Ministry of Health and the Ghana Health Service for allowing outstanding contractual obligations to result in the disruption of critical national health information systems. It also questioned Akamai’s decision to suspend the services despite the potential public health consequences, although it acknowledged that contractual obligations must be respected. The caucus has called on the Ministry to review its agreement with Akamai and consider terminating the contract where justified by the established facts and contractual provisions. Among its demands, the Minority wants government to immediately restore the affected systems and provide a clear timeline for their full operational recovery. It is also calling for a comprehensive account of GHIMS expenditure, including budgetary allocations, actual spending, implementation progress and integration with existing health information systems. Additionally, the caucus wants an investigation into the Akamai suspension to establish institutional responsibility and determine appropriate corrective action. It has proposed an independent audit of Ghana’s digital health infrastructure, covering hosting arrangements, interoperability, data security and business continuity. The Minority says sustainable financing and infrastructure safeguards must also be established to prevent similar disruptions. It maintains that Ghana’s digital health transformation must be measured by the reliability, accessibility and sustainability of systems serving the public, rather than simply the introduction of new platforms.

items.title: Présidentielle 2027 : une majorité de Français favorables à une primaire de la droite
items.description: Une majorite de Francais se declare favorable a l'organisation d'une primaire pour departager les candidats de la droite et du centre en vue de la presidentielle de 2027. Parmi les sympathisants concernes, cette proportion atteint 74 %, tandis que le maire de Cannes, David Lisnard, enregistre une nette progression. Selon l'enquete realisee les 4 et 5 novembre aupres de 1 005 personnes, 60 % des Francais souhaitent une primaire. Cette proportion atteint 74 % chez les sympathisants de droite et du centre, dont 59 % estiment qu'elle renforcerait leur camp. Les sympathisants d'Horizons y sont les plus favorables (81 %), alors meme que leur chef de file, edouard Philippe, s'oppose a cette formule, preferant une union autour de sa candidature. Ceux des Republicains (79 %) et de Renaissance (72 %) suivent de pres, tandis que Gabriel Attal , a la peine dans les etudes d'opinion, figure parmi les premiers a avoir defendu l'organisation d'une telle consultation. Concernant le perimetre de la primaire, 42 % des Francais privilegient une competition allant de Renaissance aux Republicains, en incluant Horizons et Nouvelle energie, le mouvement de David Lisnard. Les scenarios elargis a Raphael Glucksmann ou a eric Zemmour sont, en revanche, majoritairement rejetes par les sympathisants concernes. Cette demande de primaire trouve egalement un echo sur X, ou le journaliste Clement Macchi releve le fort soutien des sympathisants d'Horizons a une consultation pourtant refusee par edouard Philippe, ainsi que la progression de David Lisnard. ⚡️ Sondage choc @OdoxaSondages x @Le_Figaro 👉 Désormais 74% des sympathisants droite/centre souhaitent une primaire, et ceux qui la réclament le plus sont chez… HOR (81%), devant LR (79%) et RE (72%). 👉 Énorme progression de Lisnard. 37% (+10) des Français pensent qu’il ferait un bon candidat, seulement 2 pts derrière Philippe (39%, -8). Retailleau leader (62%, +2). — Clément Macchi (@clement_mci) November 5, 2026 Apres avoir depasse Bruno Retailleau dans les sondages fin octobre , le maire de Cannes continue ainsi son ascension. items.title: What If the Apocalypse Is Already Here?
items.description: On a patch of ground in the City of London, the exact site of the former East India Company’s headquarters, stands a puzzling structure with the nickname the “ Inside-Out Building .” Unlike the glittering, knifelike high-rises that surround it, the edifice is covered in a shell of equipment: all of the air ducts, electrical lines, elevators, and pipes run up the exterior. Inside, Lloyd’s of London, the three-century-old powerhouse firm, props up the globe’s insurers and guarantees financial security. So when a race of amorphous beings called the iGhetti arrives in England, Lloyd’s seems like a logical target. There is no better way to dominate humanity than to take over the economic heart of the empire. And there might be no better place for M. John Harrison to situate his new, Booker Prize–shortlisted novel, The End of Everything , than a building of great significance that is also irresistibly weird. The End of Everything is brief and confounding; it also doesn’t care a whit for the conventions of dystopian fiction. It’s set about 20 or 30 years in the future, mostly in the small coastal towns of Kent, where strange entities (they might be aliens, or bio-machines, or really anything) wash up onshore. The “artefacts,” as they are called, arrived around the same time as the iGhetti; together they somehow upended life as everyone knew it, rendering Britain unrecognizable within a decade. As one man, Phillip Tennent, moves through this uncanny new world order, all of the tropes of postapocalyptic fiction fall away in favor of a far more timely and provocative proposal: The apocalypse might not be an end at all, but simply a long chain of baffling, disorienting incidents. Writers have been thinking about different versions of doomsday for thousands of years—the tale of Noah’s ark is just one example of an ancient religious story about the eradication of humanity. But the fear that seems to plague modern minds is that it might all end with a whimper, rather than a bang. Through rants about late-stage capitalism , that infamous dog-in-a-fire meme , and other expressions of alarm, it’s become more and more common to hear people worrying—or joking—that the world is enduring a rolling apocalypse, a series of catastrophes so slow-moving that they won’t prevent you from browsing a J.Crew sale while everything falls apart. Because fiction favors drama, most postapocalyptic novels are structured around a single Event. In Emily St. John Mandel’s Station Eleven , Stephen King’s The Stand , and Ling Ma’s Severance , it’s a population-decimating plague; in Cormac McCarthy ’s The Road and Walter M. Miller Jr.’s A Canticle for Leibowitz , it seems to be a nuclear explosion; in Octavia Butler’s Parable of the Sower and Claire Vaye Watkins’s Gold Fame Citrus , it’s rapid, unstoppable climate collapse. Whatever the Event may be, it kicks off a transformation in how people live. Bands of survivors poke around for degrading tins of food, tribes form and fight, the remnants of modern life waste away under coats of dust and piles of rubble. There is an immovable sense of a before and an after—distinct time periods that cannot be reconciled. Harrison, however, favors inscrutability. He doesn’t make his Event an act of decimation; society keeps on going even as social structures dissolve. Characters still eat croissants, argue about World War II battles, and throw dance parties despite what they term “the disaster.” Tennent, who lives by the sea, discovers an artefact and plans to sell it. Over time, as he watches the artefact morph (it grows hands and eventually speaks), he repeatedly wonders why his country keeps changing—and how. No matter which way he turns his mind, the particulars of what has happened to Britain never resolve, as in an eye test in which each flick of the optometrist’s machinery reveals only a different kind of fuzziness. [ Read: Apocalypse, constantly ] Some facts are laid out: Europe has disappeared (one confused character makes a sign that aptly asks, HOW CAN YOU MISPLACE A CONTINENT? ); migration has reversed course and airplanes no longer fly, so Britons regularly board ferries departing for other lands. The idea of an economy is now a historical notion, and there is no government to speak of, so militias patrol the towns, but only off the page. Londoners fled the dangerous, iGhetti-occupied city, but then returned, despite the fact that the British military continued to bombard the Lloyd’s building. (Violence is a hallmark of the postapocalyptic novel, but Harrison’s characters kill with a paucity of forethought that makes McCarthy’s rogues seem like Montessori teachers by comparison.) Most facts, however, are disputed, and even the idea of a “fact” seems to have collapsed. The iGhetti might have “come out of the internet,” or they may embody “a re-enchantment of the world.” They could be aliens, or AI, or spiritual visitors. Harrison once calls them “tall writhing bursts of light” but otherwise avoids describing them as corporeal, as if they are some galactic version of Catholicism’s Holy Spirit. The term bad patch is used to describe a plot of land that’s been taken over by the iGhetti—such as the Lloyd’s building—but it is also an all-purpose term for someone who can’t see their way through the never-ending tumult. “Using the phrase in its older, pre-crisis sense,” Harrison writes, “the way you might talk about a failed marriage or career—was perhaps an unconscious attempt to normalise the inexplicable and minimise the disaster.” But what was the disaster? All Harrison will say is that there was “a decade of confusion,” and “by the time things came back into focus, the climate had changed. Geography had changed.” Nobody can even agree on whether the iGhetti are an external phenomenon or something humanity has brought upon itself. Perhaps unsurprising, all of this is a metaphor for the condition of England today . It’s no coincidence that the novel is set near Hastings, the site of the famous 1066 battle that created the modern English nation, and that the iGhetti commandeer a financial quarter that has been hollowed out by Brexit. [ Read: How Britain became as poor as Mississippi ] Yet the subject of Harrison’s experiment is larger than one referendum on territorial boundaries—or any single Event at all. He seems to be asking how humans will respond when they discover, en masse, that they are no longer in control of the planet’s destiny. Really, The End of Everything is a novel about surrender. “The apocalypse,” one character writes, “seemed to withhold itself, quickly becoming just another historical continuity. That is to say, we got used to it. No one had expected the utter banality of that.” Harrison’s sociological portrait is attuned to the common idea that disaster can quickly become boring—or all too quickly assimilated and ignored. Horrible images of global catastrophe—razed cities, drowned villages—now flit through our phones in between makeup tutorials and political punditry. Pondering barbarity or devastation is as easy as pondering a lunch menu. So what might people do if the tide turns against the whole of humanity, if the End Times finally come? In Harrison’s estimation, they’ll shrug. As bleak as this interpretation may sound, the novel is expansive rather than dismissive. It reaches out for connection, feeling at once bizarrely creative and, on a psychological level, strikingly familiar. In a short novel, in a wholly original way, Harrison has managed to sketch not just a world, but a worldview. I suspect that he knew he needed to create a new style of language and imagery to convey the emotional reality of a world “disconnected from itself.” As John Ashbery put it in 1977, “You can’t say it that way any more.” The same is true now.

items.title: Troops nab notorious terrorist in Kaduna
items.description: By: Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma, have arrested a suspected terrorist during an intelligence-led operation in Kagarko town, Kagarko Local Government Area of Kaduna State. The troops have also intensified air and ground operations to neutralise terrorists and deny them freedom of action in Zamfara State. Spokesman, Captain Tamuno Sinivie while making this known on Friday said, “On 5 November 2026, troops of Sector 1, in conjunction with operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS), apprehended a suspected terrorist identified as Auta Maikyala during an intelligence-led operation. “The suspect was arrested at a hospital in Kagarko, where he had reportedly gone to seek medical attention for a gunshot wound sustained during an encounter with a rival faction. “Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspect is an alleged notorious criminal who has been involved in several attacks on communities, kidnapping and cattle rustling operations. “He is currently in custody for further investigation and prosecution. “Similarly, troops of Operation Fansan Yamma have intensified clearance operations aimed at neutralising terrorists and dismantling their hideouts in Zamfara State. “On 5 November 2026, troops conducted clearance operations at Aljummu Hausa, Aljummu Fulani and Tunga Magaji villages in Maradun Local Government Area of Zamfara State. “The ongoing operations have resulted in the clearance of several terrorist hideouts, further restricting the activities of criminal elements and enhancing the security of residents in the affected communities. “In a related development, on the same day, the Air Component of the Nigerian Air Force, conducted air interdiction operations against identified terrorist locations suspected to be associated with the wanted terrorist kingpin, Dogo Gide, in Babban Doka and Kuyumbana Forest, Maru Local Government Area of Zamfara State. “The operation followed credible intelligence indicating that the terrorists were assembling in the area to plan and coordinate their criminal activities. “Troops are currently maintaining dominance over the general area. ‘Operation Fansan Yamma will sustain its operational tempo and aggressive posture to fulfil its mandate of protecting lives and property across the Joint Operations Area. “The general public is urged to continue supporting ongoing military operations by providing timely and credible information on suspected terrorists and their activities to assist security agencies in eliminating criminal threats from our communities.” The post Troops nab notorious terrorist in Kaduna appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Un expert | La Tunisie accuse un retard dans la transformation numérique et l’économie verte
items.description: La Tunisie accuse toujours un retard dans son processus de transformation numérique et de développement de l’économie verte, et ce, malgré la multiplicité des initiatives et des efforts déployés dans ce domaine . (Photo: Jihene El Ouakdi, marraine du Salon de l’économie verte). C4est ce qu'a déclaré Bassem Thabti, expert en transformation numérique et commissaire général adjoint du Salon de l’économie verte, de la finance responsable et du développement durable, un événement incontournable dédié aux solutions innovantes et aux initiatives en faveur d’un avenir plus durable, organisé par Néo Influence, les 5 et 6 novembre 2026, au Centre international des congrès de l’Union tunisienne de l’industrie, du commerce et de l’artisanat (Utica), à Tunis. Intervenant ce vendredi 6 novembre sur Diwan FM , M. Thabti a expliqué que la plupart des initiatives liées à ces secteurs demeurent confinées au stade des discussions et des concepts, avec une mise en œuvre concrète très limitée sur le terrain. Cette situation perdure alors même que les pays intensifient leurs efforts pour suivre les évolutions dans les domaines de la numérisation, de l’intelligence artificielle et de l’économie verte. Certaines entreprises tunisiennes ont commencé à prendre des mesures en vue d’adopter des modèles d’économie verte et d’économie circulaire ; toutefois, l’impact de ces initiatives sur le terrain demeure limité, ce qui nécessite d’accélérer le rythme de mise en œuvre et de renforcer le passage de la phase de planification à la réalisation concrète, a-t-il souligné. Selon les annonces officielles, l’année 2027 est présentée comme une étape charnière pour accentuer la souveraineté numérique, l’IA et la modernisation des infrastructures. Un Plan national 2026-2030 recense 192 projets de transformation digitale, dont on espère une réalisation rapide, mais en déplorant des pesanteurs bureaucratiques et un manque de moyens financiers. Il en de même de l’économie verte, qui est en cours de structuration à travers des stratégies nationales et des événements dédiés, mais sa mise en œuvre concrète reste confrontée à des retards structurels. items.title: ‎2027 Poll: INEC uncovers plot to kidnap ad-hoc staff, warns officers against partisanship
items.description: By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja ‎ The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has uncovered an alleged plot to threaten, intimidate and kidnap ad-hoc electoral personnel, including members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC), ahead of the 2027 general election. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, disclosed that intelligence-led operations had led to the arrest of suspected kingpins allegedly behind the plot, adding that the suspects had been charged to court through the Department of State Services (DSS). Amupitan warned that anyone who threatened or harmed electoral personnel would face the full weight of the law. He also cautioned electoral officers against partisanship and administrative negligence, insisting that personnel found wanting in the discharge of their duties would face appropriate sanctions. The INEC chairman spoke in Lokoja during the commission’s North Central zonal operational readiness assessment and interactive staff engagement, where he stressed that the credibility of the 2027 elections would depend largely on the neutrality, professionalism and commitment of personnel at the grassroots. He said the commission was strengthening collaboration with security agencies under the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) framework to identify and address potential threats before the polls. According to him, INEC is also deploying Election Risk Management tools to identify vulnerable areas across the North Central zone and share the findings with security agencies for early intervention. Amupitan said the commission was intensifying preparations nationwide to ensure that the 2027 general election was better managed than previous electoral exercises, stressing that credible polls could not be achieved through last-minute preparations. He said INEC must sustain its operational readiness through adequate logistics, technological investment, staff welfare and improved administrative processes long before election day. The chairman said the commission was preparing for an election involving more than 103 million registered voters and 176,846 polling units across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. He disclosed that the North Central zone, comprising six states and the FCT, had a combined 15.44 million registered voters, with Kogi State accounting for 1,932,654. Describing the zone as strategically important to the electoral process, Amupitan said Kogi’s geographical position and borders with several states made its logistics, security and operational readiness critical to election administration. He charged electoral officers to ensure that no eligible voter was disenfranchised through administrative lapses or logistics failures, urging them to uphold neutrality, professionalism and accountability. On the voters’ register, Amupitan said INEC was working to address irregularities identified during the display of the register for claims and objections ahead of the publication of the final register on December 15, 2026. He assured that necessary corrections would be made before the final publication. The chairman also warned that misinformation and disinformation, particularly fake news and manipulated videos circulating on social media, posed a serious threat to public confidence in the electoral process. He urged the commission’s voter education and publicity departments to intensify public enlightenment and advised citizens to verify information before sharing it. On staff welfare, Amupitan said INEC had introduced the Consolidated Election Management Body Salary Structure (CEMBSS), effective January 1, 2026, to move its workforce away from the conventional civil service salary structure. He added that an enhanced salary, hazard and field allowance package had been approved by the President, with implementation awaiting cash backing. Other measures, he said, included a 150 per cent increase in overhead allocation to state offices, improved duty tour allowances, plans for an owner-occupier housing scheme and the procurement of new vehicles, including 500 pickup trucks for logistics operations. He urged staff to see themselves as custodians of electoral integrity, saying the success of the 2027 elections would depend on their ability to uphold the law and discharge their responsibilities without fear or favour. items.title: Petrol prices set for possible November cut as crude oil drops sharply
items.description: Motorists in Ghana could see lower petrol prices from November 16 as a recent decline in international crude oil prices raises expectations of relief at the pumps, the Chamber of Petroleum Consumers (COPEC) has said. COPEC Executive Secretary Duncan Amoah says crude prices have fallen by more than 12 to 14 per cent over 48 hours, creating the possibility of a downward adjustment in the next fuel pricing cycle. However, he cautioned that the decline in crude oil prices would not immediately translate into cheaper fuel, as refined petroleum product prices typically take between six and seven days to respond to movements in the global crude market. The next pricing window opens on November 16, with the National Petroleum Authority’s guidelines requiring the use of average free-on-board prices recorded between October 27 and November 11 to determine the applicable prices. Mr Amoah said if the downward trend on the international market persists and feeds through to refined products within the assessment period, petrol prices could fall in the second half of November. “If all things are equal, and what we have observed since the mid-term elections in America happened is that you have seen prices consistently drop on the international market, our prediction or projection will be that for the second window of November, the cost of petrol, particularly, would have witnessed some reduction,” he said. Speaking on Citi FM on Thursday, November 5, he explained that the timing of the adjustment in refined product prices would determine whether consumers benefit from the November review or have to wait until December.

items.title: Uzbekistan places temporary visa ban on Nigerians
items.description: Uzbekistan has introduced temporary restrictions on visa issuance and entry for Nigerian citizens. A notice on the website of the Green Energy Technologies Central Asia (GETCA) exhibition states that restrictions have been introduced on the issuance of visas and entry into Uzbekistan for Nigerian nationals. The notice reads: “Temporary restrictions have currently been introduced on the issuance of visas and entry into the Republic of Uzbekistan for citizens of your country.” It also advises Nigerians seeking entry under exceptional circumstances to contact the consular section of the Embassy of Uzbekistan for further information. Nigeria is also not the only country listed under the temporary restrictions on the exhibition website. Other countries, including Ghana, Kenya, Egypt, Iraq and Bangladesh, also have similar notices. As of Friday, no formal public statement explaining the restrictions had been identified on the website of Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The ministry’s general visa information page provides details of the country’s visa arrangements for foreign nationals but does not specifically explain the reported restrictions affecting Nigerians. The development could affect Nigerians planning to visit the Central Asian country for tourism, business, education and other purposes. Affected travellers have been advised to contact the Uzbek embassy’s consular section to establish whether they qualify for exceptional entry arrangements. items.title: COP31: Ghana’s Climate voices must not be left behind in the accreditation queue
items.description: The controversy over Ghana’s delegation sizes at previous climate conferences seems to have created a new challenge: limiting access to the United Nations Conference of the Parties (COP) for fear of political criticism. As the world prepares for the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, from 9 to 20 November 2026, concerns are mounting among Ghanaian climate activists, civil society organisations, academics, researchers and other stakeholders over difficulties securing accreditation to participate. For many, the frustration goes beyond missing another international conference. It raises fundamental questions about representation, access and whose voices matter in shaping global climate policy. There are growing concerns that the issuance of COP badges to Ghanaian stakeholders is becoming increasingly restrictive, potentially excluding organisations and individuals whose work is central to advancing climate action. To understand the situation, it is important to revisit the politics surrounding Ghana’s participation in previous climate conferences, particularly COP26 in Glasgow and COP28 in Dubai. The politics behind Ghana’s COP delegation Ghana’s participation in COP26 attracted considerable public controversy following reports that approximately 337 Ghanaians were registered for the conference in Glasgow, United Kingdom. The figure triggered widespread criticism, with suggestions that the government was spending excessively on a large delegation at a time when the country was experiencing economic difficulties. The controversy resurfaced during COP28 in Dubai, when Ghana reportedly recorded 618 participants. However, what was often missing from these conversations was an important distinction between the number of Ghanaians registered through the UNFCCC system and the number of people officially sponsored by the Government of Ghana. At COP26, government officials clarified that the official government delegation comprised only 24 people. The wider figure included civil society representatives, journalists, academics, private sector participants and other stakeholders, all of whom financed their own participation or received support from independent institutions. At COP28, of the 618 Ghanaian participants reported, 95 appeared on the official Party list, while 523 were registered under the Party Overflow category. The fundamental problem with much of the public debate was the failure to distinguish between a country’s registered participants and its government-funded delegation. Understanding the difference: Government-sponsored delegates and Country Badge Holders One of the most persistent misconceptions surrounding Ghana’s participation in COP is the assumption that everyone registered under Ghana’s country allocation is sponsored by the Government of Ghana. This is not the case. A government-sponsored delegate is an individual whose participation, including travel, accommodation, daily allowances or other logistical expenses, is financed wholly or partly by the Government of Ghana. Such individuals are generally part of the official national delegation and may be supported with public resources to represent the country’s interests in the negotiations. A Country Badge Holder, on the other hand, refers to a participant registered under Ghana’s Party allocation through the UNFCCC accreditation system. This category can include government officials, civil society representatives, academics, researchers, journalists and private sector actors. Importantly, being registered under Ghana’s country allocation does not automatically mean that an individual is financially sponsored by the government. A person may secure a country badge through the national delegation process while independently financing their travel and accommodation, or receiving support from an NGO, development partner, private institution or another source. This distinction is critical. The number of Ghanaians recorded in the UNFCCC registration system should not automatically be interpreted as the number of people whose participation was financed by the Ghanaian taxpayer. When political criticism undermines climate action There is nothing inherently wrong with demanding accountability over public expenditure. Governments must be transparent about resources committed to international conferences, and citizens have every right to question the cost and value of official delegations. However, accountability must be based on accurate information. COP is not exclusively a gathering of presidents, ministers and government officials. It is a multilateral process that recognises the contributions of civil society organisations, research institutions, indigenous peoples, youth movements, women’s organisations, the private sector and the media. These stakeholders are not merely spectators. They conduct research, advocate policy reforms, mobilise communities, monitor climate commitments, facilitate partnerships and bring practical experiences into international discussions. Their participation at COP is often supported through independent grants, institutional budgets, development partners and personal resources. It is therefore unfortunate when their participation is reduced to a political argument about the size and cost of Ghana’s delegation. Fair and Inclusive Participation in Ghana’s Climate Diplomacy There is a legitimate question Ghana’s climate authorities must answer: Are restrictions on COP accreditation driven by genuine logistical considerations or concerns about renewed political criticism over the size of the country’s delegation? If the current approach is influenced by fears of political backlash over previous delegations under the erstwhile NPP administration, Ghana risks allowing partisan considerations to undermine inclusive climate diplomacy. Ghana’s climate challenges, from coastal erosion to illegal mining, deforestation and biodiversity loss, require the collective expertise of government, civil society, academia, the private sector and local communities. Their participation should strengthen Ghana’s climate diplomacy, not be restricted by political sensitivities or concerns about public perception. A call for inclusion Ghana must move away from turning participation in international climate conferences into a partisan political contest. Political opponents should be able to demand accountability without misrepresenting the composition and financing of national delegations. The people working to protect Ghana’s forests, restore degraded landscapes, strengthen coastal communities, and promote climate justice must not become casualties of political disagreements over delegation numbers. As COP31 beckons, the message must be clear: accountability and inclusion are not competing objectives. Ghana can pursue both. By: Emmanuel Ameyaw The writer is a Project Manager at the Africa Centre for Nature-Based Climate Action (AC4NCA)

items.title: Ayariga says IRECOP cleanup demonstrates Ghana’s capacity to tackle major waste challenges
items.description: The Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, says the ongoing clearance of waste heaps at the Integrated Recycling and Compost Plant (IRECOP) site in Accra demonstrates Ghana’s capacity to address major sanitation challenges through commitment and effective mobilisation of resources. The minister said this during a visit to the site to assess progress on the cleanup, expressing satisfaction with the visible transformation achieved so far, despite the initial 90-day deadline not having elapsed. “Today, you can see for yourselves how far we have come. That’s why I said that as a country, when we challenge ourselves, we can do a lot for ourselves,” he said. Mr Ayariga described the progress as evidence that the country could manage even its most difficult waste challenges if the necessary resources and collective commitment were brought to bear. “If we are able to clear this heap, I don’t think there’s any waste in this country that cannot be cleared. And I don’t think there’s any waste that cannot be managed,” he added. The Minister, however, stressed the need to protect the cleared land from encroachment as government works towards its proposed industrial park project on the site. “We need to protect the area as we work towards that vision,” he emphasised. He said the government also intends to cover sections of the cleared area in the interim and provide facilities, including walkways, to serve residents of surrounding communities while plans for the industrial park are pursued.
