items.title: FG seeks seven-year ban on establishing new federal universities, polytechnics
items.description: …Alausa tells Senate to stop approving establishment bills, cites NN1.3trn ASUU revitalisation debt, infrastructure deficits By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Federal Government has moved to halt the establishment of new federal universities, polytechnics and colleges of education for seven years, warning that Nigeria risks expanding its tertiary education system at the expense of academic quality and the survival of existing institutions. The government said it could no longer afford to spread scarce resources across an increasing number of institutions while existing federal tertiary institutions grapple with severe funding shortages, decaying infrastructure, inadequate manpower and overcrowded classrooms. Consequently, the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, has appealed to the Senate and other members of the National Assembly to stop considering and passing bills seeking to establish additional federal tertiary institutions during the seven-year moratorium. The appeal was contained in a November 2, 2026, memo addressed to Senate President Godswill Akpabio and copied to Senate Majority Leader Senator Michael Opeyemi Bamidele. In the memo, marked FME/DUE/NASS/153/Vol.1/147 and sighted in Abuja on Friday, Alausa disclosed that the Federal Executive Council had approved the seven-year moratorium at its August 13, 2025, meeting as part of efforts to address the proliferation of public tertiary institutions, duplication of academic programmes and under-utilisation of existing facilities. The minister’s intervention comes amid persistent concerns over the government’s ability to adequately finance existing universities, polytechnics and colleges of education, with billions of naira in outstanding revitalisation commitments yet to be met. Making a case for the policy, Alausa argued that Nigeria’s immediate challenge was no longer the multiplication of tertiary institutions but the strengthening of those already established to deliver quality education. He warned that continuing to establish new institutions without guaranteed funding would deepen the crisis in the sector, potentially leaving more institutions struggling to provide basic academic facilities and services. “The Federal Government’s position is that the immediate challenge confronting the tertiary education sector is not merely the expansion of access but the urgent need to strengthen existing institutions,” he stated. According to him, the moratorium would allow the government to consolidate previous investments, address existing deficiencies and improve the carrying capacity of operational institutions before considering further expansion. Alausa expressed concern that despite the government’s policy direction, bills seeking the establishment of additional federal tertiary institutions continued to receive legislative attention. While acknowledging the constitutional powers of the National Assembly to initiate and enact laws establishing institutions, he urged lawmakers to consider the prevailing realities of the education sector, including demonstrable national needs and the long-term financial implications of such legislation. He identified inadequate lecture halls, overcrowded classrooms, poorly equipped laboratories, shortages of qualified academic personnel, accommodation deficits and deteriorating infrastructure as some of the major challenges confronting existing federal institutions. The minister warned that creating more institutions under such circumstances would amount to spreading already inadequate resources thinner, with potentially damaging consequences for academic standards. Alausa also presented figures showing the extent of the Federal Government’s outstanding financial obligations to the university system, particularly its commitments to the revitalisation of public universities. He disclosed that of the N1.3 trillion pledged under the 2013–2018 Federal Government-ASUU revitalisation agreement, only N250 billion was reportedly released between 2013 and 2021. Similarly, he said that out of the additional N150 billion approved in 2025 for Needs Assessment Intervention, only N50 billion was initially released. The minister argued that the outstanding commitments raised serious questions about the government’s capacity to assume additional financial responsibilities through the establishment of new institutions. “These funding gaps demonstrate the difficulty of meeting existing obligations and raise legitimate concerns about the capacity to sustain additional institutions without corresponding and guaranteed budgetary provisions,” he stated. To further strengthen his argument, Alausa cited the experiences of Ekiti and Imo states, where the establishment of multiple tertiary institutions reportedly created financial and administrative challenges. He recalled that three state-owned universities in Ekiti were consolidated into one institution, Ekiti State University, Ado-Ekiti, in 2011. He also noted that Imo State had undertaken institutional reviews and integration following the establishment of several tertiary institutions under previous administrations. According to him, some state governments had also approached the Federal Government seeking takeovers of their universities because of difficulties sustaining their operations. He warned that institutions established without credible and sustainable funding arrangements could eventually become liabilities, forcing subsequent administrations to embark on expensive mergers, restructuring or outright closures. “The institutions established without sustainable funding arrangements may subsequently require costly restructuring, merger or integration by successor administrations,” he cautioned. Drawing lessons from other countries, the minister said Australia, Finland, Japan, the United States and South Africa had adopted institutional mergers and consolidation to tackle funding constraints, duplication of programmes and administrative inefficiencies. He said such reforms had helped improve institutional governance, achieve economies of scale, strengthen research capacity and ensure more efficient deployment of public resources. Alausa maintained that Nigeria needed to embrace a similar approach by placing institutional viability, academic standards and efficient resource utilisation above the continuous creation of new tertiary institutions. He further warned that the establishment of additional institutions could undermine other ongoing government interventions in the education sector, which also require substantial and sustained funding. Among the programmes he identified were infrastructure interventions by the Tertiary Education Trust Fund, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, vocational and skills acquisition initiatives, as well as the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance (CATA) and the Consolidated Tertiary Institutions Tools Allowance (CONTTA) for academic and non-academic personnel. The minister stressed that establishing a tertiary institution involved far more than enacting an enabling law, noting that such decisions imposed long-term financial obligations on successive administrations. He listed land acquisition, take-off grants, construction of infrastructure, recruitment of academic and non-academic personnel, procurement of equipment, utilities and recurrent expenditure among the costs the government must shoulder. He warned that passing establishment bills without comprehensive feasibility studies, clear evidence of national educational needs and credible long-term funding arrangements could produce institutions that exist only on paper but lack the capacity to function effectively. “Such institutions may eventually become financial liabilities, compelling future administrations to undertake costly mergers, restructuring or outright closure, with attendant consequences for students, staff, public investments and the national education system,” he stated. Rather, he said the government intended to use the period to strengthen existing institutions, improve infrastructure, address manpower shortages, raise academic standards and ensure that any future expansion was backed by adequate financial and administrative planning. He therefore appealed to Akpabio and the leadership of the National Assembly to align legislative activities with the policy. “In view of the foregoing, I respectfully appeal to Your Excellency and the distinguished leadership of the National Assembly to support the Federal Government’s seven-year moratorium by exercising restraint in the consideration and passage of Bills for the establishment of additional Federal Universities, Polytechnics and Colleges of Education during the period,” he stated. The minister maintained that the country’s educational progress should not be determined by the number of universities, polytechnics and colleges established but by their ability to provide quality education, produce competent graduates and contribute meaningfully to national development. “The success of our education system should be measured not merely by the number of institutions established but by the capacity of existing institutions to deliver high-quality education, produce competent graduates and contribute meaningfully to national development,” he added. The post FG seeks seven-year ban on establishing new federal universities, polytechnics appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Bawumia holds talks with Japanese institutions on technology, healthcare and infrastructure
items.description: New Patriotic Party (NPP) flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia has held a series of engagements with key Japanese institutions as part of his visit to the Asian country, exploring opportunities and policy approaches in technology, healthcare, infrastructure development and industrialisation. The engagements focused on how Japan has developed and applied technology and innovative policy interventions in areas such as monetary policy, digital payment systems, vaccine research and manufacturing, flood management, environmental protection and industrial development. Among the institutions he visited was the Bank of Japan, where discussions centred on monetary policy, central bank digital currency (CBDC) and the development of payment systems. The engagement provided an opportunity for discussions on Japan’s approach to central banking and the use of digital technology in financial transactions, particularly as countries continue to explore innovations in their financial systems. Dr Bawumia and his delegation also engaged officials of Japan’s Digital Agency, the institution responsible for coordinating the country’s digital transformation initiatives. The discussions examined Japan’s digitalisation efforts and the role of technology in improving public services and strengthening the delivery of government services. In the healthcare sector, the delegation met officials of Chiba University, where discussions focused on vaccine research and manufacturing. The engagement explored issues relating to scientific research, vaccine development and manufacturing capacity, areas considered important to strengthening healthcare systems and improving preparedness for public health emergencies. Infrastructure development and flood management also featured prominently in the engagements. At Japan’s Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism, Dr Bawumia and his delegation held discussions on flood prevention and river management, with attention to Japan’s approaches to managing water resources and reducing the risks associated with flooding. The discussions provided an opportunity to examine infrastructure and technical interventions that could offer useful lessons for Ghana, particularly in addressing recurring flooding and improving the management of water bodies. The delegation also met representatives of the Japan Organization for Metals and Energy Security, where industrial development and related policy issues formed part of the discussions. Another engagement was held with the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) in Japan, focusing on industrial policy and development strategies. The discussions centred on approaches to industrial development and how countries can use policy and technology to strengthen productive sectors and support economic transformation. Dr Bawumia also held discussions with the Chairman of the Research Committee on International Affairs, a member of Japan’s House of Councillors, the country’s upper parliamentary chamber. The meeting provided an opportunity for exchanges on international affairs and matters relating to cooperation between countries. Describing the engagements as fruitful and insightful, Dr Bawumia expressed appreciation to his Japanese hosts for the reception accorded him and his delegation, as well as the perspectives shared during the meetings. Bawumia explores Japanese technology for Ghana’s galamsey challenge Earlier in the visit, Dr Bawumia toured 3R, a Japanese environmental technology company specialising in sustainable solutions, where he was introduced to technologies designed to address environmental pollution. The company has developed systems capable of recycling water and treating contaminated soil through the removal of harmful heavy metals, including mercury. The technologies attracted particular interest from Dr Bawumia, given Ghana’s continuing efforts to address the environmental destruction associated with illegal small-scale mining, popularly known as galamsey. Illegal mining has contributed to the degradation of land and the pollution of water bodies, with mercury contamination among the environmental concerns associated with some mining activities. Dr Bawumia said the technology demonstrated by the company could offer valuable lessons for Ghana’s efforts to restore degraded lands and polluted water bodies. He noted that witnessing the technology in operation had reinforced the importance of adopting sustainable and innovative approaches to addressing environmental challenges. According to him, advances in environmental technology demonstrate the potential to rehabilitate damaged ecosystems, safeguard natural resources and protect future generations. He thanked the management and technical team of 3R for hosting the delegation and sharing their expertise. The engagements form part of Dr Bawumia’s broader study tour of Japan, which has focused on examining how the Asian country applies scientific research, technology and institutional policies to address development challenges. The areas explored during the visit include digital transformation, healthcare innovation, infrastructure management, environmental restoration and industrial development, with discussions centred on lessons that could inform Ghana’s development priorities.

items.title: Elon Musk appears to signal the end of the road for Cybertruck
items.description: Tesla will wind down production of its Cybertruck vehicles at its Texas factory next year, Elon Musk says. He did not spell out whether it plans to stop making them entirely or shift production elsewhere, but did say the decision was to “make room” for building more of its self-driving Cybercab cars. But the project’s lead engineer, Wes Morrill, appeared to suggest the vehicle was being discontinued, writing on X: “Cybertruck was an incredible technology development platform and lives on through Cybercab.” With its distinctive angular looks, the Cybertruck attracted diehard fans, but was beset by delays before being launched in 2023 and has had disappointing sales numbers since. Tesla fans have been mourning the news online, with one person calling it “the best vehicle Tesla has ever made” as he lamented it being “discontinued next year”. Musk responded to the user with the word “true”, adding: “But the Cybertruck fleet will be around for a long time.” The vehicle has always been a passion project for Musk. He said it was “way more awesome than people realise” in March, and called it the “best product Tesla has ever made to date” in April. But there have always been big questions about whether consumers shared that view and whether the Cybertruck could cut through and earn a spot in the US’ lucrative truck market. It was not helped by inauspicious introduction to the public in 2019 when Musk attempted to show off the Cybertruck’s apparently unbreakable glass, only for it to shatter during a live demonstration. Despite the gaffe, the Cybertruck ended up receiving a 146,000 orders, Musk said in 2019, while it was still in development. In the end, the vehicle launched in 2023, keeping its novel design – an angular shape with a body made of stainless steel. Tesla fans praised its retro-futuristic look, which some said looked like something “straight out of Blade Runner”. But critics were far less kind, joking about its appearance and labelling it “ugly as sin”. Several recalls – including in 2025 affecting more than 46,000 Cybertrucks over concerns part of its trim could fall off – would not have helped. And then there’s the price. “We need to make it at a price that people can afford,” Musk told Wall Street analysts that year – which ended up being $61,000 (then £48,000) for all the “bells and whistles”. In 2026, the so-called “Cyberbeast” model comes in at $102,000.

items.title: Mahama reaffirms Ghana’s non-aligned foreign policy amid BRICS partnership bid
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has reaffirmed Ghana’s commitment to its long-standing non-aligned foreign policy, dismissing suggestions that the country is gravitating towards the East following his recent visit to Russia and its decision to pursue a partnership with the BRICS bloc. The President maintained that Ghana’s diplomatic engagements with countries in the East should not be interpreted as a departure from its foreign policy principles, stressing that the country remains committed to maintaining friendly relations with all nations, irrespective of their political or economic orientation. Speaking during an engagement with the Presidential Press Corps following his return to Ghana from a series of international engagements, President Mahama explained that the country’s decision to pursue BRICS partnership status was consistent with its non-aligned position and did not amount to an application for full membership of the economic bloc. Quoting Ghana’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, he said: “We neither face East nor West; we face forward”, describing the statement as the foundation of Ghana’s approach to non-alignment. He questioned why his recent visit to Russia should generate concerns about Ghana’s foreign policy direction, recalling that former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo also participated in the first Russia-Africa Summit held in Sochi, Russia. President Mahama argued that Ghana’s diplomatic relationship with Russia was not a new development and should not be viewed as evidence of a shift towards the East. He further disclosed that the recommendation for Ghana to pursue a partnership with BRICS originated from a ministerial committee established under the previous New Patriotic Party (NPP) administration. According to him, the committee submitted its recommendations to Cabinet, which subsequently considered and approved the proposal under his administration. “The ministerial committee that sat and recommended that Ghana should accede to BRICS partnership was under Nana Akufo-Addo. We came and met their recommendation,” he explained. The President stressed that his administration did not establish the committee but inherited its recommendations and proceeded to approve the proposal after Cabinet considered its merits. Ghana pursuing partnership, not full BRICS membership President Mahama was particularly emphatic about the distinction between becoming a full member of BRICS and securing partnership status, insisting that Ghana was pursuing the latter. He explained that BRICS partnership provides an opportunity for countries to strengthen economic and diplomatic cooperation with the bloc without necessarily becoming full members. The President compared the arrangement to Ghana’s existing Economic Partnership Agreements (EPAs) with European countries, arguing that such international partnerships are consistent with the country’s commitment to maintaining balanced relations with different regions of the world. “We have those partnerships with many countries. For instance, with Europe, we have the Economic Partnership Agreements, EPAs. They are the same as the BRICS partnership,” he said. He maintained that Ghana’s engagement with BRICS should therefore be understood within the broader context of its international cooperation strategy rather than as an indication of geopolitical realignment. Reiterating his administration’s position, President Mahama declared that Ghana remained committed to being friends with all countries and enemies of none. “We are not drifting anywhere. We are friends to all and enemies to none,” he stated. His comments come amid growing international interest in BRICS, an intergovernmental grouping that has expanded its economic and diplomatic influence as countries seek alternatives and additional platforms for global cooperation. Ghana’s pursuit of partnership status is expected to provide further opportunities for economic engagement, trade, investment and cooperation with member countries while preserving the country’s independent foreign policy position. Government advances plans to establish a new national airline Meanwhile, the Government has announced progress towards re-establishing a national airline, following preliminary studies which have reportedly affirmed the viability of the proposed venture. A roadmap for establishing the airline has been agreed, with the process expected to involve the selection of a strategic airline partner and a technical partner, securing an Air Operator Certificate (AOC), and determining the appropriate fleet and financing arrangements. The development forms part of the government’s broader efforts to restore Ghana’s national airline capacity and strengthen the country’s position within the aviation industry. As part of the process, President Mahama on Monday held discussions with officials of Boeing Group, which is providing technical support and guidance towards Ghana’s efforts to establish a new national carrier. During the engagement, the Boeing delegation assured the President of its continued support throughout the various stages of the project, including the establishment and operational phases of the proposed airline. The company’s involvement is expected to provide technical expertise as Ghana works towards developing an airline capable of meeting international aviation standards and operating sustainably. The identification of a strategic airline partner and a technical partner will be among the critical next steps, alongside regulatory approvals, fleet acquisition and the development of appropriate financing arrangements. Although the Government has indicated that preliminary assessments support the commercial viability of the proposed airline, the successful implementation of the project will depend on securing the necessary partnerships, funding and regulatory approvals.

items.title: Tanzanian opposition leader found guilty of incitement
items.description: Tanzania’s main opposition leader, Tundu Lissu, has been found guilty of incitement in a case that has raised concerns about political freedoms in the East African country. A panel of three judges at the High Court in Dar es Salaam acquitted him of the more serious offence of treason, saying prosecutors had failed to prove a key element of that charge. The 58-year-old, who has been detained since April last year, was charged over remarks he made while campaigning for electoral reforms ahead of the disputed 2025 general election. Lissu, who leads the opposition Chadema party, has consistently denied the charges, describing the prosecution as politically motivated. He has been on trial on charges of treason and says this is the first time he has heard of the separate charge of incitement. “The offense of incitement is one that you, honourable judges, have manufactured. You have created an offense that did not exist, and you have done so on political directives,” said Lissu, when he was given a chance to address the judges. He added that he would like to apply for bail as this was possible for incitement, unlike treason. The judges are still delivering their ruling, with the legal reasoning and sentence for the incitement conviction yet to be announced. He has leave to appeal at the Court of Appeal – the country’s highest court. Treason is among Tanzania’s most serious offences and can carry the death penalty. President Samia Suluhu Hassan won the October 2025 election with 98% of the vote – a result the opposition dismissed the result as a “mockery” of democracy as her two main challengers, including Lissu, were excluded. Her government has repeatedly denied targeting its opponents. The Chadema leader was arrested six months before the poll, shortly after launching a campaign demanding changes to the electoral system under the slogan “No Reforms, No Election”. Prosecutors accused him of making statements intended to incite the public to disrupt the election and threaten the government. They argued that his remarks, which were also circulated online, amounted to treason. But Lissu, a lawyer who represented himself during the trial, maintained that his comments were part of a legitimate political campaign for constitutional and electoral reform. He argued that prosecutors had taken his statements out of context and failed to prove that he had committed any crime. Some of the demands raised by Chadema were: Electoral commissioners should be independently appointed (not by the president) Police should allow all parties to campaign free of intimidation Government-appointed district chiefs should no longer act as returning officers Party agents should be able to observe counting without harassment It should be possible to challenge presidential election results in court. During his time in remand custody at Dar es Salaam’s Ukonga Prison, Lissu went on hunger strike twice for brief periods when he said he was not allowed access to his lawyers or relatives. He also complained that guards listened to what should have been private consultations his lawyers. These allegations have been denied by the prison authorities. His case has attracted international attention, with rights groups expressing concern about the treatment of opposition politicians and the shrinking space for political dissent in Tanzania. Last year’s election was followed by widespread protests and a violent security crackdown that left at least 500 people dead, according to an official inquiry. Opposition groups have said the death toll was much higher and demanded an independent investigation. The government has defended its handling of the unrest and rejected accusations of widespread political repression. Samia, 66, has insisted the election was fair and transparent and blamed foreigners for the unrest, saying it was part of a plot to overthrow her. She has set up another commission to inquiry to identify those behind the violence. Lissu has long been one of Tanzania’s most outspoken critics of the ruling Chama Cha Mapinduzi (CCM) party, which, along with its predecessor Tanu, has dominated the country’s politics since independence. He first became an MP in 2010, representing a constituency near his birth place in Singida, 320km (200 miles) north-west of the capital, Dodoma. In September 2017, the Chadema politician narrowly survived an assassination attempt when gunmen sprayed his vehicle with bullets outside his home in Dodoma. He was shot multiple times and underwent extensive medical treatment abroad. The attack, whose perpetrators have never been brought to justice, forced him to spend years outside Tanzania. He returned to contest the 2020 presidential election against the late President John Magufuli, but lost in a vote that the opposition alleged was marred by widespread irregularities. Lissu subsequently returned to exile before coming back to Tanzania in 2023, following President Samia’s decision to lift a ban on opposition political rallies. His return was initially seen as a sign of renewed political openness after years of restrictions under Magufuli, who died in office in 2021. But relations between the government and the opposition deteriorated as the country approached the 2025 election. Lissu became Chadema’s national chairman in January 2025 and intensified his demands for electoral reforms. His conviction is likely to deepen concerns about the state of democracy in Tanzania. Last week, rights group Amnesty International accused the government of continuing its crackdown following the election and “weaponising counterterrorism laws to silence critics and instil fear”. The authorities did not respond to a request for comment.

items.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Finishing 2026 strong – The CEO’s leadership agenda
items.description: Insight. Finishing the year strong requires deliberate leadership attention. CEOs must ensure that the organisation remains focused on its most important commitments while avoiding unnecessary distractions during the final weeks of the year. This requires a clear understanding of outstanding targets, unresolved risks, customer commitments, financial obligations, and the leadership actions needed to sustain performance. The CEO must create a sense of shared responsibility for the organisation’s final results while ensuring that decisions made today do not weaken its prospects for 2027. Key Strategies: Confirm the organisation’s outstanding annual performance commitments. Prioritise activities with the greatest impact on year-end results. Strengthen executive coordination and decision-making. Protect customer relationships, employee engagement, and operational continuity. Connect final-quarter execution with the organisation’s 2027 strategic priorities. CEO Leadership Actions. Communicate a clear year-end performance agenda to the executive team. Review progress against key commitments and address obstacles promptly. Ensure short-term performance decisions support the organisation’s long-term sustainability. Actionable Tip. Ask: “What must we protect, what must we accelerate, and what must we complete to finish 2026 as a stronger organisation?” Why This Matters? The quality of year-end leadership influences both current performance and future readiness. CEOs who maintain focus, accountability, and strategic discipline help their organisations close the year with stronger results and enter 2027 with confidence. About the Author. Ernest De-Graft Egyir, CEO advisor, Thought Leader, and Founding CEO of Chief Executives Network Ghana, convenes the Ghana CEO Summit and serves on Ghana’s Economic Dialogue Planning Committee.

items.title: The Pope Confronts One of His Toughest Political Challenges
items.description: Less than a month after losing part of a lung, Pope Leo XIV set out this morning on one of the longest and most ambitious trips of his pontificate. Over the course of 11 days and 12 flights, Leo will travel from South America’s Southern Cone to the high Andes and the Amazon Rainforest. Much of the Catholic world will be focused on how its 71-year-old leader, just a few weeks removed from cancer surgery, bears the physical challenge that the trip presents. But perhaps the most important challenge he will face is political. Catholic social teaching does not line up with the ideological commitments of either the left or the right. Yet the global rise of right-wing populism has determined many of the political battles that Leo will confront as pope, particularly over the next week and a half. The center-left recently scored a victory in Brazil, but most countries in Latin America are governed by right-wing or center-right leaders, many of them populist. These include two stops on the pope’s itinerary: Argentina and his adopted home of Peru, where he served as a missionary and bishop for about two decades. Leo’s trip is an early test of how he’ll address the Church’s disagreements with the right-wing populist leaders ascendant not only in Latin America but also in Europe, the historic heartland of the Catholic Church. The emphasis he puts on either conciliation or confrontation could indicate how he’ll handle a geopolitical challenge that will shape his pontificate. Crime might be the issue that best explains the rise of the South American right. Latin America and the Caribbean together have the world’s highest homicide rate, nearly four times the global average. About half of the population of this region feels unsafe walking alone at night, compared with about a quarter of people globally, according to a Gallup survey. “There’s the violence associated with narcos fighting it out amongst themselves,” Cynthia Arnson, a fellow at the Latin America Studies Initiative at Johns Hopkins University, told me. “But then there’s the day-to-day robbery and extortion.” Arnson continued, “The right has very successfully capitalized on people’s legitimate fears and lived experience by proposing these super ironfist approaches.” The responses of right-wing leaders have created ample tension with the Church. In Argentina, Catholic bishops opposed President Javier Milei’s plan to lower the age of criminal responsibility from 16 to 14. (Milei had previously suggested that 10 might be an appropriate cutoff.) The proposal became law in February, shortly after the murder of a teenager went viral. In El Salvador, President Nayib Bukele, the self-styled “world’s coolest dictator,” has employed mass arrests and declared an extended “state of exception.” These measures have curbed the country’s once-pervasive gang violence. But as local Catholic leaders and many other critics have pointed out, they have also flouted a range of human-rights laws. [ Read: El Salvador’s exceptional prison state ] Leo has a personal understanding of Latin America’s need for security. As a missionary in Peru in the 1980s and ’90s, Leo—then Father Robert Prevost—witnessed violence by left-wing terrorists who threatened him and other clergy, John Lydon, a priest who served there with the future pope, told me. Prevost spoke out against the terrorism. But, Lydon said, he also helped organize demonstrations protesting human-rights abuses committed as part of an authoritarian counterterrorism campaign, which was led by President Alberto Fujimori. Later, as the bishop of Chiclayo, Prevost called on the former president “to personally ask forgiveness for some of the grave injustices that were committed.” Today, Peru is waging a war on crime led by President Keiko Fujimori, Alberto’s daughter, who has cited her father’s campaign as a model. Leo will be returning to the country just as her operation against cartels ramps up. Late last month, Peru’s Congress granted her administration expanded legislative powers to increase military involvement in domestic security and strengthen surveillance capabilities. Amid the national instability, Leo will visit a site with particular political resonance. In his former diocese of Chiclayo, the pope will stop at a chapel dedicated to one of Latin America’s most prominent victims of far-right violence: Saint Óscar Romero. In 1980, Romero was killed by right-wing death squads in El Salvador and later recognized as a martyr by the Church. Leo himself helped raise money for the chapel’s reconstruction. Given his wide-ranging experience in Peru, he will likely try to balance his “sympathy for the need to promote citizen security” with a commitment to the rule of law, Matthew Carnes, a political-science professor at Santa Clara University who specializes in Latin America, told me. American foreign policy under Donald Trump is bound up with the region’s emphasis on crime and the rightward shift of many governments there. According to U.S. officials, 18 countries in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Peru and Argentina, have joined Trump’s Shield of the Americas, a U.S.-led security coalition targeting drug trafficking and organized crime. The initiative is part of Washington’s regional strategy, dubbed the “Donroe Doctrine,” which aims to reestablish U.S. dominance in the Western Hemisphere. Trump’s actions in the region have drawn scrutiny from the Church. Last year, Leo questioned the administration’s military buildup off the coast of Venezuela, where the United States struck boats suspected of being used for drug trafficking. In January, a U.S. military operation toppled President Nicolás Maduro: The pope insisted that Venezuela’s sovereignty and constitution be respected. Leo has also clashed with the White House over Trump’s hard-line immigration policies, which resemble those of some Latin American leaders. In Peru, for example, Fujimori has pledged to expel undocumented immigrants, many of whom have come from Venezuela, and to use the military to police her country’s borders. Leo may use his visit to reiterate his advocacy for migrants, a consistent theme of his pontificate that he has stressed on other international trips this year, including in Spain and France. [ Read: Pope Leo’s July 4 message to America was unmistakable ] Another common feature of right-wing governments in the region is their push for a lean state, in part through cuts to social services. No leader is more emblematic of this effort than Milei, who campaigned with a chain saw to illustrate his zeal for budget slashing. Argentina’s Catholic bishops have criticized his government’s austerity policies, including cuts affecting a care home for the disabled that Leo is scheduled to visit. That stop itself could be seen as a political critique from the pope, who has called the welfare state “a genuine universal right.” Likewise, his scheduled meeting with trade unionists, business leaders, and representatives of social movements in Buenos Aires will be a natural setting for him to defend workers’ rights, a key principle of the social teaching of his namesake, Pope Leo XIII. As a presidential candidate, Milei criticized and even insulted Pope Francis, once accusing his fellow Argentine of having an “affinity for murderous Communists.” But the two held an apparently friendly meeting at the Vatican in February 2024, after Milei’s victory. Francis never visited his native land as pontiff, perhaps out of a reluctance to become embroiled in domestic politics. As a young priest, Francis had ties to the movement founded by Argentina’s longtime strongman Juan Perón, whose political heirs make up the principal opposition to the current government. Leo, by contrast, is not seen as aligned with any one movement in Argentina and will be freer to speak, Carnes said. The odd country out on Leo’s itinerary is Uruguay, which has one of the region’s few left-leaning governments. The pope may highlight the country’s robust welfare system as a model for its neighbors, Michael Shifter, a senior fellow at the Inter-American Dialogue, a Washington-based think tank, told me. But Leo will also have right-coded criticisms to make in Uruguay, one of Latin America’s most secular societies, where less than half of the population identifies with an organized religion. Last year, the country legalized euthanasia, which may prompt Leo to echo the forceful statements he recently made in France on the same issue. But there are also reasons to think that Leo may take a more restrained approach during the trip. As with much of the West, Latin America is growing more politically polarized, analysts told me. Leo, who has made unity a watchword of his pontificate, is likely “to stress the importance of reconciliation, of dialogue, of trying to overcome some of the divisions that we see in many countries,” Shifter said. “There really is no other leader in Latin America today who could do that.” Leo certainly commands unusual credibility among South Americans. The question is whether that credibility will be enough for him to draw a continent together while challenging the ideology that dominates it.

items.title: In Front of Their Noses
items.description: Truncheon-wielding, balaclava-wearing ICE agents did not swarm the polling stations. The Insurrection Act was not invoked, nor did the president order the 82nd Airborne to lock up Democratic officials. The men in leather trench coats did not slip out of black limousines at midnight to seize the editors of publications that are unfriendly to MAGA and all of its works. Annoying columnists were not forced by Proud Boys festooned with scary tattoos to drink castor oil in front of jeering mobs. Elon Musk’s hundreds of millions of dollars failed to buy the votes of masses of apathetic yokels. Instead, on Tuesday, the Republicans got a drubbing for the ages. The elections were peaceful, and their outcome so unambiguous that even Donald Trump had to accept it. For nearly a decade, a drumbeat of commentary has insisted that American democracy was teetering or indeed done: The system had been irredeemably corrupted. The gerrymanders had guaranteed a permanent Republican majority in the House. Learned scholars drew chilling parallels with Macbeth , former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, and, of course, the collapse of the Weimar Republic. Professors at Yale, giving up on the failed experiment that was America, fled for their freedom—nay, their very lives—to Canada. It was the stuff of nightmares. Just why did so many intelligent people believe that Trump had suspended the laws of political gravity, and perhaps more important, why did they think that the American people were sufficiently dumb to fall for him and MAGA indefinitely? Such reflection is difficult. At the end of 1943, George Orwell took the step—uncommon among intellectuals, and rather courageous—of rereading his diary entries from 1940 and 1941. “I find that I was usually wrong when it was possible to be wrong,” he admitted ruefully. He concluded that “to be politically happy these days you need to have no more memory than an animal.” [ Quinta Jurecic: The biggest victory of the night ] In 1946, he gave the question more careful consideration in his essay “In Front of Your Nose.” In making up one’s weekly budget, he observed, “two plus two invariably make four.” Politics was totally different, a world in which the rules of arithmetic did not apply. In the end, absurd and contradictory beliefs are “traceable to a secret belief that one’s political opinions, unlike the weekly budget, will not have to be tested against solid reality.” Just so. But tested those beliefs now have been, and it is important to ask why so many highly intelligent people refused to think that self-destructive officials and policies would self-destruct, why an appalling record of corruption, economic mismanagement, and cruelty—on top of an ill-conceived, poorly executed, and unexplained war—would not eventually yield the defeat of a party that had reliably put forward an assortment of cranks, crackpots, crooks, and careerists for the approval of the American people. The largest explanation lay in a disdain for the average American, the kind who gave Trump two chances but did not want to see noncriminal immigrants hauled off the streets or shot by masked federal agents, or the kind who thought that tariffs were stupid. This was in large measure class-based mistrust, and one wonders, even now, how fully it has been dispelled. Allied to this was a failure to appreciate the genius of a decentralized political system, in which an independent judiciary could block or retard the worst features of Trumpism until the wheels of the electoral process turned. The Republicans have made a bad start at self-examination. Vice President Vance, in a now-famous post, asserted that “our voters” showed up but voted for the other side for four reasons. He grudgingly acknowledged the economy as a general issue, but his other explanations—the Iran war, a failure to put America first, and the connection to Israel—were a set of dog whistles loud enough for humans to hear. If he could not blame the president for the Iran war, who is the natural villain? If America was not first, which country was? And Israel, well, you know. More obtuse yet: The problems he identified were focused on “our voters,” not on the American people. Vance still obsesses about the Trumpian base and seems little concerned with those outside it. The likely cratering of his chances to succeed Trump in the White House is one of the welcome consequences of this election. The challenges for the Democrats are now different. It is one thing to promise greater affordability and more social welfare, but what about an exploding and unsustainable national debt? It is fine to denounce the war with Iran, but what is the alternative? If, for example, Congress denied funding for the war, would the Democrats wish to see Iran succeed in charging tolls in the Strait of Hormuz, or, indeed, actually acquire a nuclear weapon? [ Franklin Foer: Chuck Schumer’s revenge ] The country is fortunate in having Representative Hakeem Jeffries and Senator Chuck Schumer to manage Congress: Neither overflows with charisma, perhaps, but both are highly competent parliamentary managers and reliably moderate. They will have to walk a fine line between restoring accountability in government and yielding to the thirst for revenge that besets many of their members. More broadly, the Democrats will have to figure out what things they can and should restore to a pre-Trumpian order, what things to leave alone, and in what areas they can turn the chaos of this administration into creative destruction. Above all, they will need to beware of overreach. Having listened to Democrats complain about Republican gerrymandering, I then watched them on November 3 back a constitutional amendment to allow their own gerrymander in Maryland, where I live. This will, they hope, remove the last Republican in Maryland’s delegation. They may live to learn, as the Republicans did in Texas, that in the fullness of time, such attempts to have politicians pick voters rather than the other way around can backfire. If the Democrats are to take the country in a different direction, they will have to do something else as well: explain the phenomenon of Trump. Why did he sweep into office after eight years of Barack Obama, a president who still receives unthinking and uncritical adoration on their side? How could Trump possibly have come back after four years of Joe Biden, whose mental decline they refused to see, and whose record was far more unpopular than they can yet admit? Why did the great American public—the same yokels and laborers who threw the bums out on November 3—repudiate them twice? Because if Democrats do not get the answers to those questions right, the same will, sooner or later, happen to them again.

items.title: Fire destroys 11 rooms in Anlo Town compound house
items.description: A domestic fire outbreak at Anlo Town, near the Old Slaughter House, has destroyed 11 rooms in a 23-room compound house in the New Juaben North Municipality of the Eastern Region. The Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) in a post shared on Facebook on Friday, November 6, said firefighters from the New Juaben North Municipal Fire Station responded promptly to the incident and brought the blaze under control before completely extinguishing it. A 10-member firefighting crew was deployed to the scene, where its swift intervention prevented the fire from spreading to adjoining properties. Although the remaining parts of the compound house and neighbouring buildings were spared, several personal belongings, two electric motorbikes and a bicycle were destroyed in the fire. The GNFS said access to the affected building had been restricted due to concerns about its structural integrity following the outbreak. Senior officers of the Fire Service and the Ghana Police Service subsequently visited the scene, while preliminary investigations are underway to establish the cause of the fire.

items.title: Nadra assistant director shot dead by unidentified gunmen in Peshawar's Hayatabad: police
items.description: PESHAWAR: An assistant director of the National Database and Registration Authority (Nadra) was shot dead by unidentified gunmen near the authority’s office in Peshawar’s Hayatabad area on Friday morning, police said. The official was identified as Fahad Khan, the nephew of MNA Noor Alam Khan. According to city police spokesperson Alam Khan, he was shot in an area behind the Nadra office, within the jurisdiction of Hayatabad police station. Police reached the scene after being informed of the incident and recovered eight spent .30-bore pistol casings, spokesperson Khan said. The victim’s body was shifted to a hospital for a post-mortem examination, he added. The police spokesperson added that an investigation was under way to determine the circumstances surrounding the killing and identify the perpetrators. KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi termed the incident “absolutely condemnable and unacceptable”. He said he had directed the Peshawar capital city police officer to “ensure a swift and comprehensive investigation, with no room for delay, negligence or leniency”. “Every individual involved must face the full force of the law,” he said. Later in the day, Kundi told reporters that he had spoken with the Peshawar police chief and that the suspect would be identified using surveillance cameras and arrested soon. “There were land disputes ongoing; we are looking into whether that was behind the incident, or if it was some other issue,” he said. National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq expressed “deep sorrow and regret” over the official’s demise. He also extended condolences and sympathy to the victim’s family. “The (suspects) involved in the incident should be arrested as soon as possible and brought to justice,” the NA speaker said on X. KP has seen a rise in terrorist attacks over the past year. According to the Annual Security Report 2025 from the Centre for Research and Security Studies (CRSS), KP recorded a significant surge in violence last year as “fatalities rose from 1,620 in 2024 to 2,331 in 2025”.

items.title: Wave of bomb threats afflict European flights for third time this week
items.description: A wave of bomb threats were issued to passenger flights around Europe on Friday for the third time this week, as Spain’s foreign minister said the continent appeared to be facing “hybrid aggression and a form of psychological warfare”. Hoax threats disrupted dozens of passenger flights across Europe on Thursday, forcing unplanned landings by some planes and prompting fighter jets to escort or intercept others, a dramatic escalation after an initial wave on Tuesday. No explosive devices have been found and all planes have landed safely. Danish police said on Friday they were investigating threats directed at air traffic at Copenhagen airport, but that their immediate assessment was that there had been no danger to passengers. The airport said it was “operating normally”. Czech police said they had registered bomb threats to flights departing from and arriving in Prague. An airport spokesperson said they concerned four inbound and five outbound flights, but that no explosive devices had been found and no flights had been cancelled or diverted as a result. Shortly afterwards, an Italian airport authority source said a Wizz Air flight from Prague to Rome had been diverted to Venice and landed there safely. The French prime minister’s office said four new bomb threats had been made to aircraft flying over French territory, and that all had landed safely. A bomb alert on a Ryanair flight from Rome to Lisbon prompted a security operation when it landed, CNN Portugal reported. A fire truck is parked in front of the Vaclav Havel Airport in Prague as bomb threats forced airliners to make unplanned landings across Europe, in Prague, Czech Republic, on November 5, 2026. — Reuters Hallmarks of coordinated ‘hybrid’ attack Security experts said on Thursday that the threats had the hallmarks of a coordinated “hybrid attack”, although it was always possible that individuals were issuing copycat threats or acting on personal grievances. While no country has attributed blame for the threats, ⁠they come after a wave of sabotage attacks and attempts on targets across Europe ranging from German electricity substations to defence-related facilities in the Baltic region, supermarket refrigerators in France and elsewhere and Leipzig airport in Germany. Many officials have linked the campaign to Europe’s support for Ukraine in its war against Russian invasion , accusing Moscow of a campaign of “hybrid” disruptions that are essentially cheap to execute, easily deniable, and not expected to trigger an armed response. Spanish Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares told the national broadcaster TVE that, while it would take time to determine exactly what happened, “it cannot be mere coincidence that so many incidents with exactly the same modus operandi are happening across Europe”. “The most reasonable assumption is that we are facing an attempt at hybrid aggression and a form of psychological warfare,” he said, adding that Europe must be prepared for more such challenges. On Thursday, an airport source in Italy said bomb threats had been sent to several airlines and airport operators in Rome and Milan claiming to be from “fighters of the Male State”. Reuters could not independently confirm who had sent the email and there was no immediate indication of who was behind the other threats across Europe. Vladislav Pozdnyakov, a Russian blogger who set up an anti-feminist movement called the Male State in 2016 that was later banned in Russia, said the group no longer existed and was not involved in any way.

items.title: Futsal : le Maroc s’impose face au Japon en amical
items.description: La sélection marocaine de futsal s’est imposée face au Japon (1-0), ce vendredi au Japon, à l’occasion d’un match amical disputé devant le public japonais. Dirigés par Hicham Dguig, les Lions de l’Atlas ont décroché cette victoire dans le cadre de leur préparation aux prochaines échéances internationales. Le Maroc reste sur un nouveau sacre continental après avoir remporté, en octobre dernier, la Coupe d’Afrique des nations de futsal pour la quatrième fois consécutive. Cette rencontre face au Japon constitue ainsi une étape supplémentaire dans la préparation de la sélection marocaine, qui confirme une nouvelle fois sa solidité face à un adversaire asiatique. Les deux équipes se retrouveront dimanche prochain pour une deuxième confrontation amicale, programmée à 4h00 du matin, heure marocaine. Le Maroc cherchera à confirmer lors de ce second rendez-vous, après avoir remporté le premier duel sur la plus petite des marges. items.title: ONCC : Nwokfa Chanselin prend les commandes à Bafoussam
items.description: © DR L’Agence de l’Office National du Cacao et du Café (ONCC) à Bafoussam amorce une nouvelle dynamique opérationnelle avec l’arrivée de M. Nwokfa Chaselain à sa tête. L’Agence de l’Office National du Cacao et du Café (ONCC) à Bafoussam entre dans une nouvelle phase. M. Nwokfa Chaselain prend désormais les commandes de cette structure stratégique pour la filière cacao-café dans la région de l’Ouest. Cette nomination s’inscrit dans la volonté de redynamiser l’action de l’ONCC sur le terrain, au plus près des producteurs, des coopératives et des opérateurs de la filière. À Bafoussam, carrefour économique de l’Ouest, l’agence joue un rôle central dans l’encadrement, le contrôle de la qualité et l’accompagnement des acteurs du cacao et du café. Sous la conduite de son nouveau responsable, l’agence entend renforcer sa présence opérationnelle, améliorer le suivi des campagnes et consolider la relation avec les producteurs. L’enjeu est de garantir une meilleure qualité des produits, une plus grande transparence dans les transactions et une valorisation accrue du travail des cacaoculteurs et caféiculteurs. La région de l’Ouest, avec son potentiel agricole et son dynamisme coopératif, reste un bassin important pour les deux filières. L’arrivée de M. Nwokfa Chaselain est ainsi perçue comme le signal d’une nouvelle dynamique, tournée vers l’efficacité, la proximité et la performance au service du développement de la filière cacao-café. items.title: FIFA U-17 WWC Final: Nigeria vs Japan – date, time and where to watch
items.description: Nigeria’s Flamingos will face Japan in the final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco on Saturday, November 7, as they seek to make history by winning their first title. The final, which will be the 52nd and last match of the tournament, will kick off at 7:30 p.m. Nigerian time at the Mohammed VI Football Complex, Pitch 3, in Rabat. The encounter will be the first meeting between Nigeria and Japan at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup and the first time the two countries face each other in a global final. Where to watch Nigeria vs Japan Football fans can watch the final live and for free through FIFA+, with streaming available via DAZN. How Nigeria reached the final Nigeria’s campaign in Morocco did not begin as expected, as the Flamingos suffered a 2-1 defeat to Poland in their opening group match. They subsequently recorded a narrow victory over Puerto Rico before producing one of the tournament’s biggest upsets by defeating defending champions DPR Korea 3-1. The Nigerian side built on that result with victories over Mexico and Venezuela before overcoming Brazil in the semi-finals to secure a historic place in the final. Queen Joseph was particularly impressive against Brazil, scoring a goal and providing an assist to help Nigeria reach their maiden U-17 Women’s World Cup final. Nigeria are the first African country to reach the final of the competition. How Japan reached the final Japan, meanwhile, have been impressive throughout the tournament, winning all their group-stage matches without conceding a goal. Although they fell behind against Kenya in the round of 16, Sadayoshi Shirai’s team recovered to secure a 3-1 victory. They subsequently edged Ghana to reach the semi-finals, where they faced DPR Korea. Japan came from behind in the closing stages, benefiting from a late own goal before winning the contest through a penalty shootout to book their place in a fourth U-17 Women’s World Cup final. Players to watch For Japan, Mei Hanashiro will be one of the players Nigeria must watch closely. The forward has scored four goals and provided one assist at the tournament, making her one of the team’s leading attacking threats. Nigeria will look to Queen Joseph, whose pace and attacking quality have made her one of the standout players of the competition. Her goal and assist against Brazil underlined her importance to the Flamingos’ title ambitions. What the coaches and captains said Japan coach Sadayoshi Shirai said his team were determined to complete their campaign by winning the trophy. “We don’t want to stop here. We’ll continue moving forward, prepare as well as we can for the final, and give everything we have to become world champions.” Japan captain Honoka Yotsumoto also expressed confidence ahead of the encounter. “We’ve managed to overcome barriers that had held us back for so long, one step at a time – that has given us a lot of confidence. Now we have just one more match to win, and we’re determined to make history.” Nigeria coach Akeem Busari said his team would approach the final with the same mentality they displayed against DPR Korea. “It’s just about showing the same character and playing the same way we played with North Korea, because they play with the same philosophy. They want to build the ball, they look at the high line of passes, they want their full-backs to support, so we really want to look at all that. I’m excited and I’m happy, but we just really want to pick up the trophy. That would be the icing on the cake.” Queen Joseph described reaching the final as a privilege and said the team were representing the entire continent. “I feel very happy. Playing in the final is a big privilege, representing my country in the final is a big privilege for me. I’m super proud of myself and my team because we made history. We are not here just representing Nigeria; we are here representing Africa as a whole.” Key facts ahead of the final Japan will play their 50th match in the history of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Only DPR Korea, who will face Brazil in the third-place match, have played more matches in the competition. Nigeria are the first African nation to reach the U-17 Women’s World Cup final. Japan coach Sadayoshi Shirai will become the competition’s record appearance-maker among coaches, with Saturday’s final marking his 16th match. A victory for Nigeria would make the Flamingos the first team to lose their opening match and subsequently go on to win the tournament. Vanguard News The post FIFA U-17 WWC Final: Nigeria vs Japan – date, time and where to watch appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le Président Goïta chez ses partenaires de l’AES : sécurité, circulation et développement au menu
items.description: © Internet Le président de la Transition, Assimi Goita a été reçu le 5 novembre à Niamey puis à Ouagadougou. Les deux étapes ont livré des comptes rendus officiels de précision différente. À Niamey, l’entretien en tête-à-tête entre Assimi Goïta et Abdourahamane Tiani a été suivi d’une séance de travail élargie aux délégations malienne et nigérienne. Le déplacement avait le statut de visite officielle, effectuée à l’invitation du président nigérien. Le communiqué conjoint publié à la fin des échanges cite d’abord la situation sécuritaire dans la Confédération des États du Sahel et la lutte contre les groupes armés. Les deux chefs d’État y présentent les actions de la Force unifiée de l’AES comme ayant produit des « succès ». Cette formulation constitue leur appréciation officielle. Le document ne fournit ni bilan chiffré, ni liste d’opérations, ni période permettant une vérification indépendante de ces résultats. Assimi Goïta et Abdourahamane Tiani ont également condamné ce qu’ils qualifient de tentatives de déstabilisation conduites par des mercenaires et des soutiens étatiques étrangers. Le communiqué ne nomme aucun État, aucune organisation et aucune personne. Cette accusation demeure donc une position commune des deux dirigeants, telle qu’elle figure dans le texte officiel. Circulation, transport et ressources naturelles La réunion de Niamey a aussi porté sur la coordination diplomatique entre les trois pays de l’AES. Les présidents malien et nigérien ont estimé que cette concertation avait renforcé la présence de la Confédération dans les instances sous-régionales, régionales et internationales. Sur le plan économique, le communiqué mentionne la libre circulation des personnes et des biens, les infrastructures de transport, le développement agro-industriel ainsi que l’exploitation des ressources énergétiques et minières. Il évoque des actions de coordination en cours, sans annoncer de financement, de chantier nouvellement attribué ou de calendrier d’exécution. Assimi Goïta a invité Abdourahamane Tiani à effectuer une visite officielle au Mali. Le président nigérien a accepté cette invitation. La date sera fixée par voie diplomatique. Un compte rendu plus bref à Ouagadougou Après l’étape nigérienne, Assimi Goïta a été accueilli en début de soirée à Ouagadougou par Ibrahim Traoré. La présidence du Faso a présenté ce déplacement comme une visite d’amitié et de travail. Les deux dirigeants se sont entretenus au salon d’honneur. Le compte rendu burkinabè cite le développement, la lutte contre le terrorisme dans l’espace AES, l’intégration africaine et l’actualité internationale parmi les sujets examinés. Massiré Diop

items.title: PSG : Achraf Hakimi mis au repos avant la trêve internationale
items.description: Achraf Hakimi ne disputera pas la rencontre du Paris Saint-Germain face à Troyes, prévue ce samedi au Parc des Princes, lors de la 10e journée de Ligue 1. Le latéral marocain, qui n’est pas blessé, a été mis au repos par le club parisien jusqu’au début de la trêve internationale. Le PSG a indiqué que cette décision avait été prise « en accord avec l’entraîneur et la direction sportive ». Hakimi bénéficiera ainsi d’un week-end de repos avant de rejoindre la sélection marocaine pour les deux prochains matchs des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027 face au Niger, les 13 et 17 novembre. Cette mise au repos intervient alors que l’international marocain a été particulièrement sollicité depuis le début de la saison. Le défenseur de 28 ans a participé à 14 des 15 matchs disputés par le PSG, dont 13 en tant que titulaire. Le club parisien a donc choisi de préserver son joueur avant la prochaine trêve internationale, alors que celui-ci doit retrouver les Lions de l’Atlas sous les ordres de Mohamed Ouahbi. Cette gestion individualisée de l’effectif est devenue une habitude au PSG sous Luis Enrique. Le staff parisien aménage régulièrement des périodes de repos pour certains joueurs afin de gérer leur charge physique. Ousmane Dembélé a notamment bénéficié de ce type de dispositif à plusieurs reprises, notamment en août et en octobre. Après la victoire du PSG contre Manchester City (4-2), le Ballon d’Or 2025 avait même plaisanté en évoquant des « vacances ». Luis Enrique avait alors répondu sur le ton de l’humour, avant de préciser que ces périodes de repos faisaient partie du suivi personnalisé mis en place au sein du club. Pour Hakimi, cette pause permettra donc de souffler avant de rejoindre le Maroc, où deux rendez-vous importants l’attendent face au Niger. The post PSG : Achraf Hakimi mis au repos avant la trêve internationale appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Cameroun : le MIMPMEESA et le GECAM s’allient pour faire de l’informel un levier de croissance
items.description: © DR Réunis le 4 novembre 2026 à Douala, le Ministère des PME, de l’Économie Sociale et de l’Artisanat et le GECAM ont tenu une concertation nationale pour transformer la formalisation en opportunité pour les acteurs de l’économie informelle. Comment faire de la formalisation une opportunité plutôt qu’une contrainte pour les acteurs de l’économie informelle ? C’est autour de cette problématique que le Ministère des PME, de l’Économie Sociale et de l’Artisanat (MINPMEESA) et le Groupement des Entreprises du Cameroun (GECAM) ont tenu, le mercredi 04 novembre 2026, une concertation nationale au siège du GECAM à Douala. Conduite par le Ministre Achille Bassilekin III, la délégation du MINPMEESA a pris part à cette rencontre stratégique aux côtés du Président du GECAM, Célestin Tawamba, ainsi que des administrations publiques, des collectivités territoriales décentralisées, des établissements financiers et des acteurs du secteur privé. L’objectif : identifier des solutions concrètes pour accompagner les unités de production informelles vers une économie davantage structurée, productive, compétitive et créatrice d’emplois. Au terme des travaux organisés autour de trois axes majeurs — fiscalité, structuration des filières et financement — plusieurs recommandations ont été formulées et consignées dans un communiqué final conjointement signé par le Ministre et le Président du GECAM. Ces recommandations serviront de socle à l’élaboration d’une feuille de route 2027-2030, destinée à accélérer la transformation progressive du secteur productif et à faciliter l’intégration des acteurs économiques dans les circuits formels. Pour le MINPMEESA, l’enjeu est clair : changer le regard sur les acteurs de l’informel, valoriser leur potentiel entrepreneurial et faire de leur accompagnement un véritable instrument de développement économique et social. items.title: Sperm whale spotted off Sindh's coast for first time: WWF-Pakistan
items.description: A sperm whale has been sighted off the Sindh coast for the first time, around 40 nautical miles southwest of Karachi, the World Wide Fund for Nature-Pakistan (WWF-Pakistan) said on Friday. The whale, estimated to be around 45 feet long, was encountered during an expedition by WWF-Pakistan board member Zahid Maker, the organisation said in a press release. Previous sightings of the species had been reported off the Balochistan coast in 2017, it added. Footage of the encounter showed the whale’s characteristic blowhole, distinctive skin markings and prominent hump. View this post on Instagram WWF-Pakistan Senior Director Rab Nawaz said the sighting highlighted the ecological importance of Pakistan’s offshore waters and the need to protect marine habitats and food chains that sustain large marine species. “Pakistan’s waters support an extraordinary diversity of marine life, much of which remains poorly understood and documented,” he said, calling for stronger conservation measures, responsible fishing practices and collective efforts to reduce pressure on marine ecosystems. Sperm whales primarily feed on cephalopods, including different species of squid and octopuses. In Pakistan’s coastal and offshore waters, their prey includes purpleback flying squid and diamondback squid. The mammals are deep divers, typically descending between 300 and 800 metres to forage, although they can reach depths of up to two kilometres. According to WWF-Pakistan, 26 cetacean species, including whales and dolphins, have been documented in the country’s waters. These include blue whales, Bryde’s whales and Arabian Sea humpback whales , as well as several species of toothed whales and dolphins. The organisation said its research and monitoring efforts had also helped document several toothed whale species in Pakistan’s waters for the first time. It stressed that sustained research, monitoring, sustainable fishing practices and stronger conservation measures were necessary to protect marine biodiversity in the Arabian Sea. WWF-Pakistan was established in 1970 to address environmental and conservation challenges affecting the country’s biodiversity and human population. The non-profit organisation works to protect wildlife, conserve natural resources and safeguard the environment.

items.title: Eight killed, 30 injured in bus-truck collision on Hazara Motorway
items.description: ABBOTTABAD: At least eight people were killed and 30 others injured when a passenger bus collided with a dumper truck near the Havelian Interchange on the Hazara Motorway early Friday morning, rescue officials said. The bus was travelling from Gilgit to Rawalpindi when the accident occurred. Initial reports suggested that a tyre burst caused the driver to lose control of the vehicle before it collided with the truck, the Rescue 1122 statement said. Following the incident, Rescue 1122 Abbottabad dispatched seven ambulances and a rescue vehicle to the scene to carry out relief operations. The rescue operation, led by District Emergency Officer Hafeezur Rehman, was completed successfully. Rescue personnel provided first aid to the injured before shifting them to nearby hospitals for treatment. The bodies of the eight deceased, who reportedly belonged to Gilgit, were transported to different hospitals. One body was taken to Type-D Hospital in Havelian, while four were shifted to Ayub Medical Complex and three to the District Headquarters Hospital (DHQ) Abbottabad. All 30 injured passengers, including five children and six women, were shifted to Ayub Medical Complex for medical treatment. The condition of four injured passengers was reported to be critical, added the statement. A day earlier, a collision between a passenger bus and truck claimed the lives of 11 people and left 33 others injured near Pakpattan. Last week, at least five people were killed and 27 others injured when a passenger bus plunged into a drain in Punjab’s Hafizabad district.

items.title: Cameroun/ 06 novembre : Samuel Hiram Iyodi déplore une année de « Grande désespérance »
items.description: © DR Le président du Mouvement patriotique pour la prospérité du peuple (MP3) fait le bilan de la première année du septennat des grandes espérances entamé le 06 novembre 2025 par la prestation de serment du président réélu, S.E Paul Biya. 06 novembre 2025, 06 novembre 2026, un an que le président de la République élu au scrutin du 12 octobre 2026 a pris fonction. Pour quel bilan ? Les point de vue peuvent diverger. Mais, pour le plus jeune candidat à l’élection présidentielle de 2025, c’est « année de Grande Désespérance », en référence à l’échec de ce que le slogan de campagne du candidat déclaré vainqueur a annoncé. Selon Hiram Samuel Iyodi, 12 mois après la prestation de serment « le Cameroun vit sous le règne de l'immobilisme, de l'inaction, de la précarité, du chômage des jeunes et de la multiplication des féminicides. » Dans une déclaration rendue publique ce vendredi, l’homme politique égraine le chapelet de maux qui remettent en question les engagements pris par le chef de l’Etat. Aucun bilan public du Plan spécial de promotion de l’emploi des jeunes. Pas de visibilité des 50 milliards de ce plan dans le budget de l’Etat. Pas de nomination de jeunes au gouvernement ou à la tête des entreprises publiques. Plus de 10 000 diplômés camerounais ont quitté le pays. Plus de 70 femmes et filles tuées en 2026. Le nouveau gouvernement annoncé depuis huit mois mais toujours attendu. Une croissance économique qui stagne à 3% loin des 8% prévus dans la SND30. Toutes choses qui démontrent, selon le présent du MP3 l’échec qui caractérise les 44 ans du Renouveau qui lui-même n’est pas réalisé. Parlant du bilan de ces 44 années de présidence, Hiram Samuel Iyodi voit le verre à moitié vide. « Ce qui n’a pas été accompli en quarante-quatre ans, ne pourra plus l’être ! ». Considérant que le peuple est à l’abandon, le leader politique croit pouvoir compter sur les Camerounais pour trouver la solution qui s’impose à travers les élections législatives et municipales qui s’annoncent. Cet article Cameroun/ 06 novembre : Samuel Hiram Iyodi déplore une année de « Grande désespérance » est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: « Essakane, l’oasis d’or »: de Ag Ibrahim Mohamed
items.description: • Éditée par la librairie Mercury • Préfacier par le journaliste Baba Hama • Vendu au prix de 10.000 FCFA Et de trois ouvrages en trois ans pour l’auteur Ag Ibrahim Mohamed. Le jeudi 5 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, il a mis à la disposition des lecteurs burkinabè et du monde son troisième ouvrage intitulé : “Essakane, l’oasis d’or”. Un ouvrage de 401 pages structurés en quatre grandes parties qui portent sur l’historique de la région de l’Oudalan qui a résisté à la pénétration coloniale, la ruée vers l’or d’Essakane (l’or a découverte vers les années 1984 après une période de sécheresse et choléra et les populations ont vécu cela comme une manne céleste que Dieu leur a envoyé pour leur apporter une source alternative de revenu), l’implantation de la mine industrielle après l’exploitation artisanale et semi-mécanisée qui était dirigée par l’Etat dans les années 1990 à travers la SEMOB, et la dernière partie, consacrée à la présentation de la mine d’Essakane comme un pilier industriel. Ag Ibrahim Mohamed, également journaliste a souligné que l’or est une denrée épuisable mais l’histoire de la région du Liptako Gourma et singulièrement celle du village Essakane doit être connue du public par les générations actuelles et celles futures. Et de trois ouvrages pour Ag Ibrahim Mohamed Le livre “Essakane, l’oasis d’or” a été éditée par la librairie Mercury et est vendu au prix de 10.000 FCFA. Son préfacier un grand nom du monde de la culture et du journalisme burkinabè, Baba Hama n’a pas manqué d’éloges à son ancien étudiant. Il a salué sa régularité dans la publication des ouvrages qui vient enrichir le paysage de la bibliothèque burkinabè. Sur le dernier livre, il a fait remarquer la particularité de l’auteur qui a décidé de mettre le curseur sur l’histoire du village Essakane et aujourd’hui remplacé par le site minier Essakane Gold. Le préfacier Baba a encouragé à continuer sa passion d’écriture pour davantage faire connaître l’histoire du secteur minier aux burkinabè. Il faut noter que la présentation de ce troisième ouvrage a connu la présence de nombreuses personnalités, des parents, amis et connaissances. En rappel le premier ouvrage avait pour titre « Les pépites d’or3 consacré sur la carrière de 40 femmes exécrant dans le secteur minier et le second a porté sur: « Burkina Faso : Un ténor de l’or ». items.title: INEC: 116,745 newly registered voters yet to collect PVCs in Lagos
items.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Lagos State says 116,745 Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) of newly registered voters are yet to be collected. The Administrative Secretary of INEC in Lagos, Mrs Adenike Tadese, disclosed this in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Friday. Tadese said that the commission had received 177,295 PVCs belonging to eligible residents registered during Phase One of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise in 2025. She said the commission’s weekly update as of Monday showed that 60,550 PVCs had been collected by their owners, leaving 116,745 cards awaiting collection. According to her, the uncollected cards represent a significant number of eligible voters who should collect their PVCs to exercise their franchise in the 2027 general elections. She said the cards were available for collection at the various local government offices of the commission across the state. “The cards are available for collection by their owners, not by proxy, at the various local government offices of the commission in Lagos,” she said. Tadese urged stakeholders to mobilise both old registrants who have not collected their cards and those who participated in the 2025 CVR exercise to collect their PVCs. She said the cards were still lying at INEC offices and appealed to their owners to collect them before the collection window closed ahead of the forthcoming elections. The INEC official also disclosed that PVCs belonging to eligible residents who registered during the 2026 CVR exercise before its closure would soon be ready for collection. Tadese, however, urged eligible registered voters to maintain orderliness during the collection of their PVCs. She reaffirmed the commission’s readiness to conduct free, fair and credible elections that would be acceptable to all stakeholders in the state. The administrative secretary also called for peaceful and orderly campaigns, urging all stakeholders to abide by the rules guiding the electoral process. She appealed to political actors and other stakeholders to play by the rules to ensure a peaceful electoral environment ahead of the 2027 general elections. (NAN) The post INEC: 116,745 newly registered voters yet to collect PVCs in Lagos appeared first on Vanguard News .
